Autism screening scores significantly increased following exposure to night-time heat throughout the beginning of the third trimester and possibly toward the end of pregnancy, even after adjusting for PM2.5 and PM10. During the postnatal period, night-time heat (months 2-7.5) and increased PM2.5 and PM10 exposures (months 7-11.5) led to higher scores in males compared to females. Conversely, night-time heat (months 17-20) led to higher scores in females. Our findings suggest that prenatal exposure to heat, but not air pollution, may be associated with early ASD risk indicators, while sex-specific effects of heat and PM exposure were observed in the postnatal period.

docs.title: Formal Thought Disorders.
docs.text: Formal thought disorder (FTD), changes in the form (as opposed to the content) of thinking, has a largely unknown pathophysiological basis or bases, although language, frontal/executive, and semantic memory mechanisms have been implicated. FTD is a major symptom of schizophrenia and is also common in mania, with there being a marked overlap of clinical features between the 2 disorders. Changes in thought form are also seen in major depression, autistic spectrum disorder, and the frontal lobe syndrome; the presentations in these latter disorders differ from those seen in schizophrenia and mania, notwithstanding some points of overlap.
docs.venue: The Psychiatric clinics of North America

docs.title: Instruments and scales for assessment, screening, and psychoeducational diagnosis of children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder: a scoping review.
docs.text: Objective: To investigate instruments and scales for psychoeducational assessment, screening, and diagnosis of children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder. Data Source: This review followed the methodological procedures recommended by the Joanna Briggs Institute and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses - Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). Its research question was, "What are the main instruments and scales for psychoeducational assessment, screening, and diagnosis of children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder in school?". Data Synthesis: The study included 16 articles that investigated instruments for psychoeducational assessment, screening, and diagnosis of children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder. The instruments found were the Psychoeducational Profile - Revised (PEP-R), Psychoeducational Profile 3 (PEP-3), and the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children (WISC-IV). This indicates a scarcity of instruments and scales for the psychoeducational assessment, screening, and diagnosis of children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder. Conclusions: The most used instruments to assess the psychoeducational profile of schoolchildren with autism spectrum disorder include the Revised Psychoeducational Profile (PEP-R) and the Psychoeducational Profile, 3rd Edition (PEP-3), according to scientific literature. There is a scarcity of instruments and scales for the psychoeducational assessment, screening, and diagnosis of children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder, suggesting the need for further research on the subject.
docs.venue: Revista paulista de pediatria : orgao oficial da Sociedade de Pediatria de Sao Paulo

docs.title: Opposing Patterns of the Histone Variant MacroH2A1.1 in Fmr1 Knockout and BTBR T+ Itpr3tf/J Mouse Models of Autism Spectrum Disorder.
docs.text: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) exhibits substantial heterogeneity, wherein genetic and idiopathic forms may converge on shared core phenotypes through divergent molecular pathways. The histone variant macroH2A1.1, implicated in chromatin repression and DNA repair, has been linked to behavioral alterations opposite to core ASD features when depleted systemically. However, its regional and cell-type-specific regulation in genetic versus idiopathic ASD models remains unclear. We investigated macroH2A1.1 expression across the dorsal striatum, hippocampus, and medial prefrontal cortex in Fmr1 knockout (Fragile X syndrome model) and BTBR T+ Itpr3tf/J (idiopathic ASD model) mice. Quantitative PCR and imaging analyses revealed opposing patterns: BTBR mice showed region-specific mRNA downregulation and increased strongly stained macroH2A1.1-positive nuclei, whereas Fmr1 knockout mice exhibited reduced strong staining with increased weak staining, specific to neurons and not astrocytes, independent of significant mRNA changes. Bulk RNA-seq meta-analysis and pseudobulk single-cell transcriptomics further identified pathway-level enrichment of oxidative phosphorylation, chromatin remodeling, and transcriptional repression functional gene sets in unmatched public datasets (BTBR striatum; FXS hippocampus and cortex), with pronounced neuron-astrocyte divergence in Fmr1 knockout cortex. These findings underscore distinct epigenetic regulatory mechanisms in genetic and idiopathic ASD models.

docs.title: Deep brain stimulation of the nucleus basalis magnocellularis ameliorates autistic behavior in a rat model of autism via cholinergic modulation in the prefrontal cortex.
docs.text: Objective: In the present study, we investigated whether deep brain stimulation (DBS) of the nucleus basalis magnocellularis (NBM) improves autism spectrum disorder (ASD)-related behavioral abnormalities in a valproic acid (VPA)-induced rat model of autism, consistent with changes in cholinergic markers in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC). Methods: On the 12.5th day of gestation, pregnant rats ( n = 16) received a single intraperitoneal injection of 500 mg/kg sodium valproate dissolved in 0.9% saline, while others ( n = 5) received saline alone. Male offspring were allowed to reach 3 months of age and then were randomly assigned to one of four experimental groups: Contr - prenatally saline injected, VPA - prenatally VPA-injected, VPA/I - VPA-injected with electrode implantation in the NBM, and VPA/S - VPA-injected with electrical stimulation. DBS was initiated in rats of the VPA/S group 10 days after surgery (two consecutive hours per day, every day for 2 weeks; DBS parameters: 60 Hz, 120 µs, and 50 µA). Results: The prenatally VPA-exposed rats demonstrate deficits in social behavior, increased locomotor activity, and reduced anxiety levels. Immunohistochemical evaluation shows a decrease in the number of acetylcholinesterase-immunoreactive neurons in the mPFC and choline acetyltransferase-immunoreactive neurons in the NBM. NBM-DBS improves VPA-induced autistic behavior and increases the number of acetylcholinesterase-immunoreactive neurons in the PFC. Conclusion: The correlation between ASD-like behavior and cholinergic markers in the mPFC supports our hypothesis that NBM-DBS improves behavioral deficits by modulating cholinergic neurotransmission in the PFC in a rat model of autism.

docs.title: Smoking cessation interventions in adults with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) or autism spectrum disorder (ASD).
docs.text: This is a protocol for a Cochrane review (intervention). The objectives are as follows: Primary objective To assess the effects of smoking cessation interventions, compared with no intervention, usual care, placebo, or alternative interventions, on sustained abstinence from smoking in adults with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), autism spectrum disorder (ASD), or co-occurring ADHD and ASD. Secondary objectives To assess whether the effects of smoking cessation interventions differ between adults with ADHD, ASD, and co‑occurring ADHD and ASD. To assess whether intervention effects vary according to participant characteristics (e.g. ADHD or ASD symptom profiles, co‑occurring mental health conditions, and alcohol- or substance-use disorders). To assess the safety and acceptability of smoking cessation interventions, including serious and non-serious adverse events and treatment discontinuation.
docs.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews

docs.title: Acetaminophen-induced liver injury triggers short- and long-term neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier disruption, and behavioral deficits in a genetic mouse model of autism.
docs.text: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition with a strong genetic basis, yet its etiology is not fully understood. Neuroinflammation is emerging as a critical secondary factor. Since peripheral organ injury, such as acute liver failure, can induce neuroinflammation, we aimed to investigate whether liver injury could exacerbate ASD-like phenotypes in a genetically susceptible model. We used adult (12-month-old) Shank3-/- mice, a genetic model of ASD, and their wild-type (WT) counterparts. A single high dose of acetaminophen (APAP; 350 mg/kg) was administered intraperitoneally to induce acute liver injury. We assessed acute (24-h) and long-term (1-month) consequences on liver health, neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier integrity, and brain edema using plasma biomarkers, immunohistochemistry, and in-vivo MRI, as well as behavioral phenotypes, including sociability, repetitive behaviors and exploration. Acutely, APAP induced severe liver damage, cerebral edema, and neuroinflammation in Shank3-/- mice. One month later, despite liver recovery, both APAP-treated WT and Shank3-/- mice exhibited brain edema, elevated apparent transverse relaxation (R2*) rates, and lasting neuroinflammation, evidenced by microgliosis and reactive astrocytosis. These differences were more extensive in the Shank3-/- group. Behaviorally, this was accompanied by increased social deficits in both genotypes. Critically, only the APAP-treated Shank3-/- mice displayed significantly increased repetitive behaviors, and reduced exploratory activity. Here, we show that transient liver injury is associated with long-term neuroinflammation, markers of blood-brain barrier disruption, and behavioral deficits. These findings demonstrate that while peripheral organ damage can induce lasting behavioral changes in healthy animals, the severity and spectrum of these deficits are exacerbated by ASD-associated genetic predisposition. These findings support a preclinical gene-environment interaction framework relevant to ASD-associated vulnerability.

docs.title: Autism with social anxiety is associated with acquiescent behaviors and enlarged amygdala volume.
docs.text: Social anxiety (SA) frequently co-occurs with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), but it remains unclear whether SA in ASD reflects greater symptom severity or a distinct subtype. Across two complementary studies, we characterized the behavioral and neural correlates of SA in ASD using a naturalistic social navigation task measuring affiliative and power-related behaviors. In Study 1 (ASD = 575; controls = 357), autistic individuals with SA exhibited significantly reduced task-derived power behaviors (e.g., compliance with others' requests) compared to those without SA-a pattern not observed in non-autistic individuals. In Study 2 (ASD = 72; controls = 72), individuals with both ASD and SA showed enlarged amygdala volumes relative to both ASD without SA and non-autistic individuals. These behavioral and neural differences found in Study 1 and Study 2 were not observed in ASD with co-occurring depression or generalized anxiety disorder. Moreover, in Study 2, larger amygdala volume in the ASD group was associated with reduced task-derived power behaviors, indicating a neural signature linking social-behavioral differences and anxiety-related features. Together, these findings point to a distinct ASD phenotype marked by social anxiety, altered interpersonal dynamics, and amygdala enlargement, with implications for diagnosis and tailored intervention.

docs.title: Evolutionary Weighted Hodge Laplacian Descriptors for rs-fMRI Brain Networks.
docs.text: Complex biological networks often exhibit multiscale organization that is not fully characterized by pairwise edge weights or fixed graph summaries, motivating compact descriptors that retain both topological and spectral information. Here, we present an evolutionary weighted Hodge Laplacian (EWHL) framework for resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) connectivity, in which the functional connectivity matrix of each subject is represented as a weighted Vietoris-Rips filtration and 0-dimensional and 1-dimensional weighted Hodge Laplacian spectral descriptors are extracted across 13 positive connectivity thresholds. In an autism spectrum disorder (ASD) classification task using 884 participants from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange I (ABIDE I) cohort, EWHL reduced the original 6670-dimensional functional connectivity vector to 130 features and, with eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), yielded 87.7% accuracy and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.946 under 20 repetitions of 10-fold cross validation. Under the same internal protocol, EWHL outperformed a rerun raw functional connectivity baseline and a single threshold ablation, suggesting that multiscale weighted Hodge spectra provide informative descriptors for functional brain networks derived from rs-fMRI, although confound control within each fold and external validation remain necessary before clinical interpretation.
docs.venue: Journal of chemical information and modeling

docs.title: Global organization of structural covariance networks derived from parcellated cortical surface area in atypical populations.
docs.text: Higher-order features of brain organization are powerful measures for understanding the relationship between brain and experience. In particular, the global arrangement of structural features of the cortex provides insight into neurodevelopmental processes that underlie individual differences in perception and cognition. Structural covariance networks (SCNs), which capture regional coordination of brain morphometry, are an efficient method to derive global cortical properties. However, their interpretation relies on an array of methodological choices that are often inconsistent between studies. Using a hierarchically clustered version of the Human Connectome Project (HCP) atlas, we constructed SCNs of regional cortical surface area for groups with four different conditions-synesthesia, autism, early psychosis, and anxiety or depression-and compared global network properties with those of age- and sex-matched controls. SCNs for synesthesia and autism showed globally stronger connectivity, with specific increases at moderate cortical distances, as well as lower network complexity. Conversely, the SCN for early psychosis showed a globally lower connectivity and a greater complexity, while depression and anxiety showed few differences compared with controls. The results for autism and depression were replicated across two datasets each. These findings support the notion that synesthesia and autism share neurodevelopmental mechanisms, while psychosis may involve a diverging process.

docs.title: Online gaming for autistic youth: Exploring the impact on participation from the perspectives of autistic adolescents and their caregivers.
docs.text: Introduction: The rise in the number of adolescents diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder has highlighted the need for strength-based approaches to support them. The accessibility of online gaming has made it a popular avenue for autistic adolescents to socialise and connect with others while enhancing skill development. This study aimed to explore online gaming from the perspectives of autistic adolescents and their caregivers, including the impact gaming may have on daily participation and functioning. Methods: This study employed a mixed methods research design. Both autistic adolescents and their caregivers completed online surveys comprising a combination of Likert-scale and open-ended questions. The survey responses were descriptively and thematically analysed. Consumer And Community Involvement: Survey questions were reviewed by volunteer staff (including autistic staff members) of a local autistic community coding club to ensure readability and accessibility of the survey. Results: In total, 45 participants (23 caregivers and 22 autistic adolescents) responded to the survey. Themes relating to online gaming were identified, including social communication, emotion regulation, and skill development while also highlighting caregiver concerns of online safety and excessive screen use. Most autistic adolescents reported feeling happy when playing online games and most caregivers agreed online gaming supported their child to build better relationships with others. Over half of autistic adolescents agreed that online gaming helped them feel more confident in social situations with others. Conclusion: Allied health professionals, including occupational therapists, may utilise online gaming, incorporating strength-based learning and skill development, when working alongside autistic adolescents and their caregivers to facilitate social participation and promote online safety.

docs.title: KATNAL2 dysfunction impairs microtubule dynamics and contributes to syndromic neurodevelopmental disease.
docs.text: Katanins are microtubule-severing ATPases. Dysfunction of katanin subunits has been implicated in impaired neurogenesis, morphogenesis, and neuronal migration. Although heterozygous variants in KATNAL2 (katanin-like 2), a known autism-spectrum disorder (ASD) risk gene, have been reported in patients with ASD or other neurodevelopmental disorders (NDD), the underlying cellular mechanisms remain incompletely defined. Whole-exome sequencing (WES) identified a homozygous missense variant in KATNAL2 (NM_001387690.1:c.1390T>C; p.(Ser464Pro)) in a pediatric patient presenting with severe global developmental delay, intellectual disability, infantile-onset epilepsy, and autistic features, extending the phenotypic spectrum beyond prior autism-focused associations. To elucidate the cellular mechanisms underlying KATNAL2 dysfunction, we established induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) from patient fibroblasts and differentiated them into neural progenitor cells (NPCs) for quantitative immunofluorescence analyses of microtubule organization, microtubule regulatory proteins, and transcriptome profiling. In parallel, we generated CRISPR/Cas9 katnal2 zebrafish crispants and assessed body patterning and axonal projections using the transgenic nbt:dsRed line. Patient iPSC-derived NPCs showed impaired interphase microtubule network organization with increased angular standard deviation in directionality and mitotic/cytokinetic abnormalities, including abnormal positioning of the microtubule-rich cytokinetic midbody region. In vivo, CRISPR/Cas9 katnal2 zebrafish crispants showed abnormal body patterning together with disorganized motor neuron and posterior lateral line nerve axonal projections. Together, these findings support KATNAL2 as a regulator of microtubule network organization and mitotic progression in human NPCs. Our data from patient-derived NPCs and a zebrafish model provide functional evidence linking the p.(Ser464Pro) variant to an expanded syndromic neurodevelopmental phenotype.

docs.title: Single-Cell Integration of Mouse Models of Autism Reveals Conserved Transcriptomic Signatures of Excitatory-Inhibitory Imbalance and Glial Dysfunction.
docs.text: The etiological heterogeneity of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) complicates identifying core molecular mechanisms. We systematically integrated scRNA-seq data from 11 diverse genetic and environmental mouse (Mus musculus) models, encompassing > 300,000 cells across multiple brain regions and developmental stages. Using advanced computational harmonization (RPCA), we identified robust convergent transcriptomic signatures that transcend model-specific variability. Our findings reveal widespread alterations in neuronal communication pathways, specifically increased excitatory-inhibitory signaling involving PTN, SLIT, and PTPR pathways. Furthermore, cell-cell communication analysis via NicheNet prioritized ligand-receptor pairs associated with altered circuit excitability, offering a predictive blueprint of dysregulated intercellular crosstalk. Crucially, we identified significant glial involvement characterized by astrocyte function inhibition, marked by Aqp4 and Kcnj10 downregulation related to impaired water/potassium homeostasis and mature oligodendrocyte metabolic dysregulation through Olig family upregulation and enhanced oxidative phosphorylation. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) significantly overlapped with SFARI-listed high-confidence risk genes, particularly within excitatory neuronal subtypes. Comparison with human postmortem single-nucleus data from the prefrontal and parietal cortices demonstrated conserved signatures related to impaired synaptic protein synthesis (GRIN2B, CAMK2A) and oligodendrocyte-mediated neurodevelopmental deficits (NRXN, DLGAP). This study confirms that E/I imbalance and glial dysfunction are universal cellular pathologies in ASD, providing a robust, large-scale reference for identifying novel therapeutic targets with single-cell resolution.

docs.title: Bridging language phenotypes, neural dynamics and gene regulation in autism.
docs.text: Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASDs) affect approximately 1% of the global population, with prevalence rising over recent decades. Although ASDs are heritable (~70%), translating genetic findings into effective therapeutics remains challenging due to the vast number of implicated risk genes (>700) and the limited influence of individual genes on disease expression. Their collective impact and convergent expression patterns of small-effect genes provide insights into ASD-related neurobiological mechanisms. Current interventions remain symptom-focused and do not address underlying neurodevelopmental mechanisms. Emerging approaches in functional genomics offer new insights into ASD pathogenesis by exploring gene expression diversity, yet clinical applications remain distant. Language deficits are among the most frequent and disabling features of ASD, profoundly affecting individuals' and families' quality of life. Recent evidence from neuroimaging and electrophysiology studies suggests disrupted neural oscillatory dynamics are linked to language deficits in ASD. Several ASD-associated genes have been implicated in biological pathways involved in the regulation of brain oscillatory dynamics, suggesting a potential mechanistic link between genetic variation, altered brain rhythms, and language impairment. We propose a neurophysiological imaging genetics framework that leverages neural oscillatory profiles as endophenotypes for targeted investigation and as functional readouts of gene expression. Within this framework, neuromodulation is proposed as an experimental approach to investigate and potentially modulate altered oscillatory dynamics associated with speech communication deficits in ASD, while integrating oscillation-related ASD candidate genes into a symptom-oriented model of functional genomics. This approach shows how integrating genetic variation, non-invasive neuroimaging, and behavioral phenotypes can advance our understanding of ASD and inform targeted, mechanism-based interventions.

docs.title: Misophonia in adolescents: clinical correlates and associations with autism-related behavioral characteristics within a clinical context.
docs.text: Background: Misophonia is characterized by intense emotional and behavioral reactions to specific sounds and has been associated with psychiatric symptoms and sensory sensitivity. This study investigated the prevalence of misophonia in a clinical adolescent outpatient sample and examined its associations with psychiatric symptoms and autism-related behavioral characteristics. Methods: The study included 200 adolescents aged 12-18 years who were referred to a child and adolescent psychiatry outpatient clinic. Psychiatric diagnoses were assessed using the Kiddie Schedule for Affective Disorders and Schizophrenia for School-Age Children-Present and Lifetime Version for DSM-5. Misophonia severity was evaluated with the Amsterdam Misophonia Scale-Revised, while emotional-behavioral problems and autism-related behavioral characteristics were assessed using the Youth Self-Report/11-18. Group comparisons were performed using the chi-squared test, Fisher's exact test, and the Mann-Whitney U test. Spearman's correlation analyses and hierarchical logistic regression analyses were conducted. Results: Adolescents with misophonia had higher rates of major depressive disorder. They also had significantly higher internalizing and externalizing symptoms and elevated autism-related behavioral characteristics than those without misophonia (all p < 0.001; Z = -5.62, -4.59, and - 5.70, respectively). Hierarchical logistic regression analysis revealed that higher internalizing problem scores independently predicted the presence of misophonia (Nagelkerke R² = 0.226, p < 0.001; OR = 1.07). Conclusions: Misophonia in adolescents appears to be closely associated with broader internalizing psychopathology and emotional-behavioral difficulties within psychiatric outpatient settings. Elevated autism-related behavioral characteristics in adolescents with misophonia support further research into the relationship between misophonia and neurodevelopmental characteristics. Such research may contribute to improving clinical assessment and understanding of behavioral patterns associated with misophonia. However, study limitations and inconsistencies in the literature highlight the need for further research in this area.

docs.title: Impact of socioeconomic factors and birth-related conditions on autism spectrum disorder, Down syndrome, and attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder.
docs.text: Background And Objective: This study examined the association between socioeconomic factors and maternal birth-related variables in children diagnosed with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), Down Syndrome (DS), and Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD). Methods: A retrospective analysis was conducted using data from King Khalid University Hospital Riyadh between 2015 and 2024. The sample included 269 children: 185 with ASD, 51 with DS, and 33 with ADHD. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify significant predictors. Results: Maternal use of medications during pregnancy (excluding dietary supplements) was significantly associated with a higher likelihood of ASD (OR = 4.253, p = 0.012). Child age was also significant, with each additional year increasing ASD odds by about 5% (OR = 1.054, p = 0.040). Child birth order played a role, as first- or second-born children were less likely to be diagnosed with ASD compared to later-born children (OR = 0.660, p = 0.002). For DS, higher socioeconomic status index (SESi) was linked to a reduced risk, with each unit increase in SESi score, DS odds decreased significantly (OR = 0.578, p = 0.018). Maternal employment during pregnancy was associated with increased DS odds (OR = 1.535, p = 0.024). In contrast, maternal vitamin D supplementation was associated with reduced odds of DS (OR = 0.452, p = 0.028). Regarding ADHD, assisted conception was the only factor significant predictor. Children conceived through assisted reproductive methods had more than twice the likelihood of ADHD compared to those conceived naturally (OR = 2.401, p = 0.040). Conclusion: Maternal medication use during pregnancy was associated with increased ASD risk, while birth order and child age also played roles. For DS, higher socioeconomic status reduced risk, whereas maternal employment increased it and vitamin D supplementation was less associated with the disorder. Assisted conception was the only factor linked to increased ADHD risk. Overall, maternal, socioeconomic, and perinatal factors showed distinct associations across ASD, DS, and ADHD.

docs.title: Effectiveness and Influencing Factors of Drama-Based Interventions for Social Skills in Children and Adolescents with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Meta-Analysis.
docs.text: Deficits in social skills are a core challenge for children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). This meta-analysis examined the effects of drama-based interventions on social skills in this population and explored potential moderators. A systematic search was conducted in Web of Science, PubMed, ProQuest, EBSCO, and CNKI. Overall effects were estimated using Hedges' g, and subgroup analyses and meta-regressions were conducted to examine heterogeneity. Publication bias and sensitivity analyses were also assessed. Sixteen controlled studies involving 703 participants contributed data to the meta-analysis. Drama-based interventions showed a significant medium effect on social skills (g = 0.54, 95% CI [0.21, 0.88], p = 0.002), with substantial heterogeneity (Q(15) = 62.59, p < 0.001; I² = 76.04%). Drama approach (Q(2) = 10.78, p = 0.005), intervention setting (Q(2) = 11.30, p = 0.010), and intervention agent (Q(2) = 6.64, p = 0.036) significantly moderated effects. Participant age was not a significant moderator, and dosage indicators were not significantly associated with effect sizes. These findings suggest that drama-based interventions may support social skills in autistic children and adolescents, with effects varying by intervention organization and delivery context.
docs.venue: Research on child and adolescent psychopathology

docs.title: Autism: epidemiology, genetics, molecular mechanisms, clinical features, diagnosis, and management.
docs.text: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a lifelong neurodevelopmental condition characterized by persistent deficits in social communication and restricted, repetitive behaviors. Global prevalence has risen steadily, yet reported rates vary markedly across regions and populations. These discrepancies reflect inequities in diagnostic access and screening capacity rather than true differences in incidence. This review integrates recent advances across the full ASD research spectrum. We first examine global epidemiological patterns and demographic disparities. We then dissect the genetic architecture of ASD, including rare and common variants, copy number variations, and gene-environment interactions that disrupt prenatal and early postnatal brain development. At the molecular level, diverse risk factors converge on shared neurodevelopmental mechanisms. These include synaptic dysfunction, dysregulated signaling through mTOR, Ras-ERK-MAPK, Wnt and Notch pathways, impaired neurogenesis, chronic neuroimmune inflammation, and excitatory-inhibitory imbalance. We also discuss how these mechanisms manifest in core clinical features, including social deficits, repetitive behaviors, and sensory abnormalities. We summarize current diagnostic standards and their limitations. Cross-species animal models, from Drosophila to non-human primates, are evaluated for their essential roles in mechanistic validation and therapeutic screening. Finally, we assess clinical management strategies, ranging from behavioral and educational interventions to pharmacological and supportive services. By tracing a continuous path from risk factors at the population level through molecular pathophysiology to interventions guided by mechanism, this review offers an integrative synthesis that connects basic discovery to clinical translation. We further discuss how multi-omics and artificial intelligence may advance precise diagnosis rooted in mechanism and personalized treatment.

docs.title: Aging in Autism: An Event-Related Potentials Study of Auditory Change Detection.
docs.text: Autistic individuals are often thought to exhibit reduced tolerance for change, which may stem from atypicalities in sensory processing, particularly in the detection of environmental changes. Within the predictive coding framework, this intolerance may reflect altered generation and updating internal predictions in response to sensory input, leading to increased prediction errors. Mismatch negativity and the P3a component are event-related potentials (ERPs) indexing automatic auditory change detection and involuntary attention shift. While studied in autistic children and young adults, little is known about how these components evolve during aging, an important gap as 21 million autistic adults over 60 are expected by 2050. This study examined mismatch negativity and P3a responses in 43 autistic adults (aged 21-64) and 60 nonautistic adults (aged 20-69) using a passive auditory oddball paradigm with standard (1000 Hz) and deviant (1100 Hz; p = 0.15) tones. Electroencephalography recording revealed no significant differences between autistic and nonautistic individuals on mismatch negativity and P3a amplitude or latency. However, mismatch negativity amplitude decreased with age over frontal site, similarly across both groups. No age-related effects were found for mismatch negativity latency or P3a measures in either group. These findings suggest that, from adulthood onward, the neural mechanisms underlying automatic change detection and preattentional processes are similar in both autistic and nonautistic adults, and that their overall time course of aging appears comparable, supporting the parallel aging hypothesis. Nonetheless, future research should explore how these preserved neural responses relate to behavioral reactivity to change in autism.

docs.title: Screen use, parent-child interaction, and social interaction behaviors in autistic children.
docs.text: The rapid expansion of digital technologies has transformed children's everyday environments, raising concerns about excessive screen use and its potential developmental implications. Although research on screen use has increased substantially, relatively little is known about how screen use may relate to family interaction processes among autistic children. The present study aimed to examine the relationships among screen use, autism severity, parent-child interaction behaviors, and children's social interaction behaviors in autistic children. The study employed a correlational research design. Participants included 784 parent-child pairs recruited from multiple provinces across Türkiye. Data were collected through a demographic questionnaire, the Autism Behavior Assessment Tool (ABAS), and parent-reported measures of children's screen use patterns. In addition, observational interaction data were obtained from a subsample of 102 mother-child dyads using the Maternal Behavior Rating Scale-Turkish Version (MBRS-TV), the Child Behavior Rating Scale-Turkish Version (CBRS-TV), and the Social Interaction Assessment Instrument (SIAI-TV). The findings indicated that children's screen use was positively associated with autism severity and autistic interaction behaviors, while negatively associated with attention, interaction initiation, and overall interaction behaviors. Maternal interaction behaviors were positively associated with children's interaction behaviors and negatively associated with children's screen use. These results suggest that higher levels of screen exposure may be related to reduced social interaction opportunities among autistic children. Overall, the findings highlight the importance of considering family interaction processes when evaluating digital media use in autistic children and suggest that balanced media routines and responsive parenting may support healthier developmental outcomes.

docs.title: Mapping the interplay of intelligence, empathy, systemizing, and autistic traits in children with and without autism spectrum disorder.
docs.text: Background: Intelligence, empathy, systemizing, and autistic traits are psychological dimensions that vary continuously across the population. Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) may reflect extreme expressions of these traits, yet their interdependencies and difference between typically developing (TD) children remain poorly understood. Methods: We recruited 186 children with ASD and 364 TD children aged 6-12 years. Intelligence was assessed using the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children-Fourth Edition, while empathy, systemizing, and autistic traits were measured using validated Chinese versions of the Empathy Quotient, Systemizing Quotient, and Autism Spectrum Quotient. Undirected partial correlation networks and Bayesian networks were estimated separately for each group, adjusting for demographic covariates, including gender, parental education level, and household income. Results: Across groups, cognitive empathy consistently emerged as the central hub in both undirected and Bayesian network analyses. In ASD, autistic traits formed a densely interconnected cluster with limited cross-domain links, while in TD children they were more flexibly integrated with systemizing and other domains. Intelligence formed a cohesive yet relatively independent subnetwork, though in ASD verbal comprehension was directly predicted by social communication competence. The estimated networks demonstrated robust accuracy and acceptable stability. Conclusion: These findings reveal both shared and distinct patterns of network organization among intelligence, empathy, systemizing, and autistic traits in children with and without ASD. Cognitive empathy may represent a potential target for future intervention research, while systemizing tendencies and cognitive strengths may also inform individualized support strategies in ASD.

docs.title: Working memory and language development have a bi-directional longitudinal relationship in autistic preschoolers.
docs.text: Background: Among neurotypical children working memory and language development are closely related, but the longitudinal relationship between these factors is unknown in autism. This study had the goal of evaluating potential bidirectional relationships between these domains. Methods: A longitudinal design included language and visuospatial working memory assessments across three time points with 160 autistic preschoolers. Time points were one year apart. A cross-lagged panel model (CLPM) using Full-Information Maximum Likelihood (FIML) was used to evaluate longitudinal associations between performance on a working memory task (i.e., the Hide and Seek Task) and language scores (i.e., verbal development quotient). Results: Cross-lagged associations were significant for paths from working memory at the first time point to language at the second time point (β = .31, p = .01) and from language at first time point to working memory at the second time point (β = .40, p < .001). Cross-lagged paths from the second to third time point were not statistically significant in either direction. Conclusions: This study provides evidence of a bidirectional relationship between working memory and language in autistic toddlers and preschoolers among younger autistic preschoolers. These results highlight working memory as a potential early assessment and intervention domain for improving language outcomes in autism as well as the role of language delays as a factor related to reduced working memory skills later in development.

docs.title: Caregiver-implemented standardized-to-individualized behavior-analytic toilet-training package for preschoolers with autism.
docs.text: Children with autism often face challenges with incontinence and may benefit from more structured toilet training relative to neurotypical children. In the current study, we evaluated a standardized-to-individualized behavior-analytic toilet-training package with caregivers as the interventionists. We used telehealth to train caregivers remotely to support their implementation of the procedures and obtain additional data on implementation and outcomes. Four preschool-aged children with autism and their caregivers participated. Three of four participants met mastery criteria with a standardized toilet-training package and one participant required a contingent progressive sit schedule. Intervention components were successfully faded, and all participants maintained performance after 4 weeks. The findings demonstrate that clinic-based toilet-training procedures can be implemented at home by caregivers with telehealth support. This approach to toilet training provides families with an alternative to clinic-based treatment and could increase access to treatment among those residing in rural or underserved areas.

docs.title: Automated screening of autism via a pretrained vision-language model in naturalistic caregiver-child interactions.
docs.text: Early autism screening is essential for timely intervention but remains constrained by specialist dependence, costly protocols, and limited accessibility. We present Autism-CLIP, a vision-language model that automates screening from 3-min naturalistic caregiver-child interaction videos recorded in toddlers aged 15-24 months. By integrating contrastive learning, large language model-generated supervision, domain-specific architecture, and hybrid training, Autism-CLIP aligns visual behavioral cues with autism-related assessment outcomes, enabling annotation-free inference. In multicenter evaluation, Autism-CLIP achieved an AUC of 0.903 in the internal cohort (n = 103) and 0.873 in the external cohort (n = 102), outperforming conventional machine learning methods. Attention mapping highlighted clinically relevant markers, including gaze aversion and limited social reciprocity. Requiring only smartphone-captured videos without manual coding or controlled settings, Autism-CLIP offers a scalable, low-cost approach to broaden access to early autism screening and support prioritization of clinical resources.

docs.title: Comparative effects of non-pharmacological intervention categories on cognitive domains in children with autism spectrum disorder: A systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
docs.text: This systematic review and network meta-analysis aimed to compare the effects of non-pharmacological intervention categories on attention, working memory, comprehensive executive function, and social-emotional cognition in children with autism spectrum disorder. Five databases were searched for randomized controlled trials published from January 2005-12 April 2026. Random-effects pairwise meta-analyses and frequentist network meta-analyses were conducted using standardized mean differences with 95% confidence intervals. Risk of bias and confidence in network estimates were assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool and CINeMA, respectively. Thirty-six reports met the eligibility criteria, and 35 reports involving 1694 children contributed to the quantitative synthesis. Non-pharmacological interventions produced a statistically significant moderate overall improvement in cognitive outcomes (standardized mean difference = 0.54, 95% confidence interval 0.36-0.71), with significant benefits for working memory (0.61, 0.09-1.13) and social-emotional cognition (0.47, 0.30-0.65). Social-emotional cognition was the only domain with a sufficiently connected network for comparisons across intervention categories; social-behavioral and technology- and robot-assisted interventions showed the clearest benefits relative to active controls. Evidence networks for attention, working memory, and comprehensive executive function were sparse or disconnected. Confidence was moderate for selected social-emotional cognition comparisons but low or very low for most estimates. Non-pharmacological interventions may improve selected cognitive outcomes in children with autism spectrum disorder, but effects appear domain specific. More adequately powered head-to-head trials using standardized outcomes are needed.

docs.title: Beyond heartbeats: re-thinking interoception in autism through virtual reality and computational modelling.
docs.text: Interoception, the sensing and interpretation of internal bodily signals, is increasingly invoked to explain heterogeneity in autism, yet empirical findings remain inconsistent. A major reason is methodological: the field remains cardio-centric and relies heavily on heartbeat counting tasks and trait questionnaires, which are vulnerable to cognitive strategies, attention, expectancy effects, and confounds such as alexithymia and anxiety. Autism research further indicates that interoception is multidimensional (accuracy, sensibility, metacognitive awareness) and developmentally dynamic, with evidence for dissociations across components and compensation across the lifespan. We argue that progress requires reframing interoception as an inference problem: the brain estimates hidden physiological states from noisy sensory evidence under context-dependent precision weighting (predictive processing/active inference). Building on this framework, we propose a participatory, multimodal research program for autism that integrates (i) lived experience as hypothesis-shaping data, (ii) virtual reality (VR) as an experimental testbed to manipulate embodiment, sensory load, agency cues, and feedback, and (iii) computational physiological modelling to estimate latent cardiovascular-respiratory and autonomic-control parameters, which could subsequently constrain separately specified models of perceptual inference.

docs.title: Past, present, and future of non-pharmacological interventions for autism spectrum disorder: A global bibliometric and thematic analysis (2001-2025).
docs.text: Background: Non-pharmacological interventions (NPIs) have become increasingly important in addressing the complex and heterogeneous needs of individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), particularly in light of the limitations associated with pharmacological treatments. Objective: This study aimed to systematically map the global research landscape and thematic evolution of NPIs for ASD from 2001 to 2025 using bibliometric approaches. Methods: A total of 341 English-language articles were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. Microsoft Excel and Biblioshiny were employed to perform descriptive analysis, co-authorship network mapping, keyword co-occurrence analysis, and thematic evolution analysis based on Keywords Plus. Results: The findings indicate a sustained increase in research output, particularly after 2011, with publication volume peaking in 2024 and citation impact continuing to rise. Music therapy, applied behavior analysis, and repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation emerged as the most influential intervention approaches. The United States led in both publication volume and academic impact, followed by China and the United Kingdom. Thematic evolution analysis revealed a gradual shift from behavior-oriented frameworks toward mechanism-informed and context-sensitive approaches, with increasing attention to early intervention, population heterogeneity, and family involvement. Conclusion: Research on NPIs for ASD is undergoing a transition toward more integrative, individualized, and evidence-based paradigms. Future studies should prioritize longitudinal designs, cross-cultural validation, and the translation of mechanistic insights into scalable, real-world interventions.

docs.title: The active self in autism: multisensory and sensorimotor foundations of bodily self-representation.
docs.text: The active self, understood as the embodied sense of self arising from goal-directed action and interaction with the environment, is supported by sensorimotor processes including multisensory integration and proprioception. Atypical self-representation in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) has been proposed to relate to differences in these processes. To clarify this relationship, we conducted a systematic conceptual review of 37 empirical studies published between 2010 and August 2025 examining multisensory and bodily components of the active self in ASD. The literature was synthesized across three themes: (1) multisensory integration, (2) self-bias and self-other differentiation, and (3) motor underpinnings of bodily awareness. Across studies, autistic participants frequently showed differences in multisensory timing and weighting, including reduced or delayed susceptibility to some bodily ownership illusions and greater reliance on proprioceptive or immediate sensory information. Evidence also indicated differences in the flexibility of peri- and interpersonal space, self-other differentiation, agency-related processing, and motor planning and execution. However, findings were not uniform across paradigms, developmental stages, or participant groups, with relatively preserved performance reported under some unimodal or low-noise conditions. Together, these findings support an association between multisensory and sensorimotor processing and several components of bodily self-representation in autism, while substantial methodological and sample heterogeneity limits strong causal or clinical conclusions. Future research should prioritize larger and more representative samples, longitudinal and multimethod designs, standardized experimental paradigms, and objective measures of embodiment to determine whether these mechanisms can ultimately inform individualized assessment and intervention.Clinical trial number Not applicable.

docs.title: NLGN3 autism variants have distinct functional impact on synapses and sleep behavior in Drosophila.
docs.text: Neuroligin-3 (NLGN3) was first identified as a X-linked risk gene associated with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Most reported variants are identified in males who inherited their variants from an unaffected mother, but de novo variants have also been identified in both affected heterozygous females and hemizygous males. The p.R451C variant was the initial variant associating NLGN3 with ASD and has been heavily investigated, yet little is known about the functional consequences of other NLGN3 variants. To determine the functional consequences of other NLGN3 variants in vivo, we generated transgenic Drosophila models corresponding to a de novo variant (p.R175W) identified in a heterozygous female proband with ASD, a maternally inherited variant (p.R451C) identified in a hemizygous male with ASD, and another maternally inherited variant identified in a male (p.R597W) associated with sleep disorder and ASD. In Drosophila, loss of the fly homolog, Nlg3, altered sleep patterns, synaptic architecture, and vesicle dynamics, which were rescued by the expression of the human NLGN3Ref allele. When comparing the variants, the p.R175W variant and the maternally inherited p.R451C variant altered synapse morphology with minimal effects on vesicle dynamics, and the p.R597W variant altered sleep and vesicle dynamics with minimal impact on synapse morphology. Using overexpression models, human NLGN3Ref altered sleep patterns and synaptic morphology. Moreover, the p.R175W variant exacerbated sleep phenotypes, and the p.R175W and p.R451C variants exacerbated synapse morphology phenotypes. Together, our findings suggest that the de novo NLGN3 p.R175W variant identified in a heterozygous female exhibits gain-of-function properties, while maternally inherited variants have context-dependent functional impact. Moreover, some NLGN3 variants disrupt synaptic development, while other variants alter synaptic function, suggesting that NLGN3 variants have differential effects. These functional differences may provide insight into the heterogeneity of individuals with ASD.

docs.title: Electrodermal Activity as a Metric of Arousal in Autistic Children Prior to Dental Treatment.
docs.text: Several prominent theories have asserted atypical arousal as a biological feature of autism. However, there is mixed evidence regarding atypical arousal patterns, particularly resting-state arousal, in autistic children, with research increasingly using psychophysiological measures, such as electrodermal activity (EDA), to help elucidate arousal levels in individuals who might not otherwise be able to identify such states. This study analyzed extant EDA data from 135 autistic children (6-12 years) collected during a baseline rest period in a dental environment to determine the relationships between tonic (mean skin conductance level; SCL) and phasic (frequency of non-specific skin conductance responses; NS-SCRs) arousal and participant characteristics, including sensory over-responsiveness, autism traits, expressive language, and general anxiety. EDA data were collected using pre-gelled electrodes placed on the distal phalanges of the participant's non-dominant hand using the BIOPAC MP150 system. Data preprocessing and epoch analyses were conducted using BIOPAC AcqKnowledge software. Conditional linear and, for the outcome variable anxiety, quadratic growth models were used to assess the temporal (within-participant across observations) relationship between EDA and behavioral variables. The results revealed a significant time-by-autism trait interaction for SCL, as well as linear and quadratic relationships between anxiety and NS-SCRs. No significant relationships were found between EDA arousal parameters and sensory over-responsiveness or expressive language abilities. A significant covariance relationship between SCL and NS-SCR frequency was also observed. Collectively, these results support previous characterizations of unique, within-autism-population arousal profiles related to autism traits, anxiety, and tonic-to-phasic covariance patterns.

docs.title: Phenotypic Complexity and Diagnostic Utility of Exome Sequencing in ASD: Real-World Insights from Colombia.
docs.text: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a genetically heterogeneous condition; however, genomic data from Latin American populations remain limited. We investigated the molecular and phenotypic landscape of ASD in 916 Colombian patients who underwent whole-exome sequencing (WES) between 2022 and 2025. Clinical and genomic data were retrospectively analyzed, and phenotypes were standardized using Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) terms. Variants were classified per ACMG/ClinGen guidelines, and we assessed phenotypic burden, predictors of molecular diagnosis, copy number variants (CNVs), and functional convergence of candidate genes. A molecular diagnosis was identified in 112 patients (12.2%), including 82 with variants in ASD-associated genes or regions and 30 with findings related to other clinical features. We identified 16 novel pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants, along with 10 CNVs. Among trio-based patients, 70.9% of molecular diagnoses were de novo. Higher phenotypic burden was associated with molecular diagnosis, and global developmental delay was the strongest predictor after correction for multiple testing. Functional enrichment analysis of candidate genes showed convergence on pathways related to neuronal development, synaptic function, and ion transport. These findings highlight the genetic and phenotypic heterogeneity of ASD and support the value of integrating standardized genomic and phenotypic characterization in Colombian populations.

docs.title: Construction of Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) for Triphenyl Phosphate (TPHP)-Induced Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and Risk Identification of Neurodevelopmental Toxicity of Aryl Organophosphorus Flame Retardants (OPFRs) Based on Multidimensional Bioinformatic Data.
docs.text: Triphenyl phosphate (TPHP) is a widely used plasticizer and organophosphate flame retardant extensively applied in various industrial and consumer products. Due to its pervasive environmental exposure and detection in human samples such as amniotic fluid and breast milk, TPHP has become a pollutant of significant concern in recent years for its potential neurodevelopmental impacts on humans. This study employed a multimethod approach integrating network toxicology, transcriptomics, in silico gene knockout, molecular docking, and molecular dynamic simulations to investigate TPHP's potential toxic role in autism spectrum disorder (ASD). An adverse outcome pathway (AOP) was constructed, revealing that TPHP exposure may induce and exacerbate ASD by downregulating GAD1-the core gene encoding the GABA synthesis rate-limiting enzyme (glutamate decarboxylase)-leading to an excitation-inhibition imbalance in the brain. The batch molecular docking of 85 organophosphate flame retardants (OPFRs) (widely detected in human and biological matrices) with the GAD1 protein identified aryl-OPFRs as disruptors targeting GAD1 to induce neurodevelopmental toxicity. In summary, this research provides mechanistic insights into how TPHP promotes ASD progression and offers a valuable chemical reference for assessing the neurodevelopmental toxicity of OPFRs.

docs.title: Cord-Derived Stem Cells for Pediatric Autism Spectrum Disorder: Biological Rationale and Source-Specific Trial Design.
docs.text: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) affects approximately 1 in 31 children, yet no pharmacological agent targets its core symptoms, leaving a substantial therapeutic gap. Umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (UC-MSCs) have emerged as a biologically rational candidate, because their immunomodulatory, anti-inflammatory, and neurotrophic properties align with the chronic neuroinflammation, peripheral immune dysregulation, and microglial overactivation that characterize ASD pathophysiology. This review synthesizes the mechanistic rationale, tissue-source biology, manufacturing and characterization standards, preclinical evidence, and clinical trial landscape for cord-derived cell therapy in pediatric ASD, and examines administration routes, post-treatment monitoring, and long-term safety. Across five published clinical trials employing cord blood mononuclear cells, autologous and allogeneic umbilical cord blood, UC-MSCs, bone marrow-derived MSCs, and Wharton's jelly-derived MSCs, short-term safety is the most consistent finding, whereas efficacy remains unresolved owing to small sample sizes, single-arm designs, and heterogeneous outcome measures; a completed randomized Phase II trial of a cord tissue MSC product, reported to date only in the trial registry, did not meet its primary endpoint. The central argument advanced here is that the proposed active component of cord-derived therapy is the purified MSC population rather than the heterogeneous mononuclear cell fraction; this proposition is supported by the CD14+ monocyte mechanism and by the one pediatric trial in which purified UC-MSC was added to a mononuclear preparation, but it has not been confirmed in any clinical study and remains a hypothesis. Advancing the field requires dedicated source-specific randomized controlled trials integrating product standardization, patient stratification, and dose-route-timing optimization.

docs.title: Ophthalmologic manifestations in children with autism spectrum disorder.
docs.text: Purpose: To determine the frequency and clinical characteristics of ophthalmologic manifestations in children aged ≤16 years with autism spectrum disorder who were evaluated at a private academic healthcare network and a public tertiary hospital. Methods: This retrospective descriptive study was conducted through a review of the medical records of children aged <16 years with autism spectrum disorder who were examined between 2023 and 2024. Demographic characteristics, visual function testability, refractive errors, strabismus, and prescribed treatments were analyzed. Dynamic retinoscopy was used to objectively assess the binocular accommodative response. Statistical analyses included 95% confidence intervals (Wilson score method) and exploratory multivariate logistic regression. Results: A total of 144 children were included; 79.2% were male, and the mean age was 6.3±2.7 years. Refractive errors were identified in 81.9% of children, of whom 63.2% had clinically significant errors requiring optical correction. Strabismus was diagnosed in 32.6% of cases, with exotropia being the most prevalent type. Stereopsis was successfully assessed in 72.2% of children. Notably, dynamic retinoscopy demonstrated perfect agreement (κ=1.000, p<0.001) with the presence of clinically significant refractive errors. Multivariate regression showed that increasing age was strongly associated with successful visual acuity testing, whereas neurological comorbidities and greater autism spectrum disorder severity significantly increased the odds of non-testability. Among children who continued follow-up, 63.9% experienced significant improvement in visual acuity. Although optical correction was generally well tolerated, adherence to occlusion therapy was notably low (6.8%), and 42.4% of the cohort was lost to follow-up. Conclusions: Ophthalmologic abnormalities, particularly refractive errors and strabismus, are highly prevalent among children with autism spectrum disorder. Given the limited reliability of subjective visual assessment in this population, objective measures, particularly dynamic retinoscopy and cycloplegic refraction, are essential for accurate diagnosis. The substantial loss to follow-up further highlights the need for adapted clinical strategies to ensure continuity of ophthalmologic care in this population.

docs.title: Two clusters of brain regions with distinct age-related profiles of functional connectivity in autism spectrum disorder.
docs.text: Brain functional connectivity changes throughout development, and individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) may follow trajectories that differ from those of typically developing controls. Using large multisite resting-state fMRI cross-sectional datasets, we examined how functional connectivity differences between ASD and typically developing controls change across a broad age range of 5 to 64 y. A data-driven analysis identified two spatially distributed clusters of cortical regions showing distinct age-related profiles of ASD-TD connectivity differences. Cluster 1 was marked by consistent hypoconnectivity across ages, suggesting a stable neural signature of ASD. Cluster 2 was characterized by hypoconnectivity in childhood that gradually diminished with age, suggesting a temporary delay profile. These clusters were systematically organized along the sensory-association axis. Cluster 1 mainly involved lower-rank sensory and sensorimotor cortices, while Cluster 2 mainly involved higher-rank association cortices. Brain-behavior analyses revealed greater and broader ASD symptom associations across ages in the consistent hypoconnectivity profile than the delay profile. Further subtype analyses suggested that social-affect symptoms were associated with greater hypoconnectivity than repetitive behavior symptoms in both clusters. Spatial correlation analyses with neurotransmitter maps revealed associations of Cluster 1 with mGluR5 and of Cluster 2 with GABAAα5, providing insight into the neurobiological basis of the two clusters. In a cross-disorder validation analysis, applying the same analytic framework to attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder did not reveal comparable results. Together, these findings suggest that ASD-related functional connectivity alterations are developmentally heterogeneous and organized along the cortical hierarchy, providing a developmental perspective for understanding the neurobiology of ASD.
docs.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

docs.title: Syndromic Autism in Helsmoortel-Van der Aa Syndrome: From Clinical Suspicion to Genetic Diagnosis.
docs.text: Syndromic autism refers to autism spectrum disorder (ASD) occurring as part of an identifiable genetic syndrome. Helsmoortel-Van der Aa syndrome (HVDAS/ADNP syndrome) is a rare autosomal dominant neurodevelopmental disorder caused by heterozygous pathogenic variants in the ADNP gene. We report a 10-year-old boy with ASD and intellectual disability who exhibited delayed motor and language development, characteristic facial dysmorphism, early tooth eruption, endocrine abnormalities, electroencephalography (EEG) abnormalities, and urogenital findings. Following unremarkable karyotyping and chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA), whole-exome sequencing identified a heterozygous pathogenic de novo frameshift variant, c.1239_1240del, p.(Gln414Valfs*25) in ADNP. This case emphasizes the importance of considering a syndromic etiology in children with ASD accompanied by developmental delay, dysmorphic features, neurological findings, or multisystem involvement, and supports comprehensive genetic evaluation when first-tier testing is unrevealing.

docs.title: Preoperative Sedation via Cecostomy Tube in an Autistic Adolescent: A Case Report.
docs.text: Preoperative sedation of autistic children is frequently complicated by challenges in communication, sensory processing, and participation in medical care. We report a 40-kg, 13-year-old autistic boy with a preexisting cecostomy tube for chronic constipation, in whom previous oral and intramuscular sedation had failed due to agitation and physical aggression. Midazolam 10 mg (0.25 mg/kg) and ketamine 200 mg (5 mg/kg) were administered via cecostomy tube, producing sedation within 20 minutes. Dental rehabilitation under general anesthesia proceeded uneventfully. Cecal administration of sedatives may be a feasible option when conventional routes are poorly tolerated, although absorption, dosing, and reproducibility remain uncertain.

docs.title: To Collapse or not to Collapse Multiple Measures of the Same Psychological Construct: A Demonstration Across 14 Independent Studies of Autistic and Non-Autistic Children.
docs.text: Large data repositories provide a valuable opportunity to combine multiple independent studies, creating large samples that can address questions not achievable within a single study. However, independent studies often use different instruments to measure the same behavior or psychological construct, such as cognitive ability, social functioning, or psychopathology. Investigators often combine samples that include different instruments under the assumption that instruments assessing the same construct capture the same underlying phenomenon. Yet this assumption of instrument interchangeability may be wrong. Collapsing different instruments into a single variable could introduce bias. Here, we established a quantitative method to demonstrate compatibility among multiple instruments with moderation analyses. We illustrate this method in domains of cognitive ability, anxiety symptoms, and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder symptoms as exemplars that might interact with outcomes of interest (autistic features instruments). A total of 1,352 participants were included from autistic and non-autistic samples across 14 independent studies. Our findings suggest that within this sample, some commonly used instruments within a domain can be acceptably combined, whereas others demonstrate discrepant relationships with outcomes of interest. More importantly, we offer a generalizable approach for scientists seeking to leverage existing datasets for secondary analyses.
docs.venue: Research on child and adolescent psychopathology

docs.title: A Comprehensive Toolkit to Support Self-Report Questionnaires for Autistic Adults With Cognitive Disability.
docs.text: Objectives: Autistic individuals with cognitive disability are underrepresented in research using self-report measures. This study aimed to develop a toolkit of customizable accommodations to facilitate self-report and to explore its usability through implementation with quality of life (QoL) questionnaires. Methods: A consultation process in three rounds was conducted with 10 experts in autism and/or cognitive disability to identify accommodations. The resulting accommodations were implemented with QoL questionnaires (WHOQoL-BREF-ID, WHOQoL-DIS-ID, ASQoL). Twenty-two autistic participants with cognitive disability, accompanied by a parent, completed the questionnaires. Feedback interviews explored participants' experiences with the accommodations. Results: Sixty-four accommodations and a cross-cutting concern: the need for a flexible protocol were retained in the toolkit. Feedback supported the usefulness of several accommodations while highlighting areas for improvement. Conclusions: This toolkit facilitates self-report among autistic individuals with cognitive disabilities, which is crucial for valid QoL assessments and development of relevant services.
docs.venue: Journal of applied research in intellectual disabilities : JARID

docs.title: Functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy Combined with Machine Learning for Exploratory Classification of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Young Children.
docs.text: Early identification of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) may facilitate timely intervention, while diagnosis remains clinically based. This exploratory study evaluated fNIRS-derived features using multiple machine-learning algorithms to compare observed classification performance between young children aged 2-6 years with ASD and typically developing (TD) children. β-activation values from eight channels were used as features to differentiate the ASD and TD groups. Two paradigm-specific analytic datasets were analyzed. Paradigm 1 comprised three tasks and included 60 participants (29 children with ASD and 31 TD children), with 24 β features per participant. Paradigm 2 comprised two tasks and included 58 participants (28 children with ASD and 30 TD children), with 16 β features per participant. Leave-one-out cross-validation was used to partition the data, and normalization and principal component analysis were applied for feature extraction. Seven classifiers-K-nearest neighbors (KNN), logistic regression (LR), support vector machine (SVM), decision tree (DT), random forest (RF), gradient boosting decision trees (GBDT), and XGBoost-were evaluated using accuracy, specificity, sensitivity, and area under the curve (AUC), and permutation testing was used to assess whether the observed classification performance exceeded that expected by chance. In Paradigm 1, KNN yielded the highest observed accuracy (0.567), whereas DT yielded the highest observed AUC (0.582). Paradigm 2 yielded numerically higher observed performance for several metrics, but no classifier significantly exceeded chance. These findings demonstrate the procedural feasibility of acquiring and analyzing task-based fNIRS data; however, independent diagnostic value beyond age and sex was not established and requires validation in larger, sex-balanced external cohorts. Overall classification performance was modest; none of the evaluated classifiers demonstrated statistically significant above-chance performance in the permutation tests, and the fNIRS features did not demonstrate statistically significant incremental predictive value beyond age and sex.

docs.title: Structure-based discovery of a novel Granzyme A (GZMA) inhibitor for autism spectrum disorder through integrative transcriptomics, virtual screening, and long-timescale molecular dynamics simulations.
docs.text: Granzyme A (GZMA) is a trypsin-like serine protease expressed in cytotoxic lymphocytes that cleaves gasdermin B (GSDMB) to release a pore-forming N-terminal fragment, thereby inducing pyroptosis, a lytic and pro-inflammatory form of programmed cell death. This pathway has been implicated in immune dysregulation reported in a subset of individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). In this study, we reanalyzed the peripheral blood transcriptome dataset GSE26415 using an integrative computational framework comprising outlier-aware quality control, differential expression analysis, functional enrichment profiling, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and protein-protein interaction network centrality scoring. These orthogonal evidence layers were integrated into a composite prioritization score, in which GZMA ranked first among candidate genes, followed by KLRK1 and KLRB1. Querying the Drug-Gene Interaction Database revealed no approved small-molecule inhibitors targeting GZMA, indicating that it remains pharmacologically undrugged. To explore druggability at the structural level, we performed structure-based virtual screening of a ZINC similarity library against the active site of GZMA (PDB ID: 1ORF). This yielded three drug-like candidates (T1, T2, and T3) with docking scores of -9.3, -9.1, and -8.9 kcal/mol, respectively, compared with -7.4 kcal/mol for the co-crystallized reference ligand (0G6). Each drug-protein complex and apo enzyme was studied in 500 ns molecular dynamics to verify the binding stability and conformational persistence compared to the unliganded protein. Among the screening compounds, T2 was able to occupy the catalytic pocket for the entire simulation, with a stable protein-ligand interaction and one low-energy conformational basin. T1, despite a better docking score, was able to detach from the pocket after around 400 ns, while T3 was able to do so in 50 ns. The overall order of binding persistence was T2 > T1 > T3. Collectively, these results prioritize GZMA as a key ASD-associated immune effector candidate and identify T2 as the most credible lead compound. Importantly, the findings underscore the limitation of docking scores alone and demonstrate that long-timescale molecular dynamics simulations and binding free energy are essential for distinguishing kinetically stable binders from transient docking poses. We note that GZMA was transcriptionally downregulated in peripheral blood; its selection rests on network centrality and on the premise that granzyme pathology is governed by enzymatic activity at tissue sites rather than by circulating transcript abundance, a mechanistic hypothesis to be tested at the activity level.

docs.title: Metallothionein-Related Findings in Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review and Targeted Quantitative Synthesis of Human Studies.
docs.text: Metallothioneins (MTs) are cysteine-rich proteins that regulate zinc (Zn) and copper (Cu) homeostasis, bind toxic metals, and contribute to redox control. Disturbed trace-element status, oxidative stress, gastrointestinal disease, and immune alterations have been reported in autism spectrum disorder (ASD), raising the question of whether MT biology is altered in this condition. Systematic searches of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, Cochrane CENTRAL, and APA PsycINFO were updated on 5 September 2026. Studies directly measuring circulating MT protein, MT isoform mRNA, or anti-MT immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibodies in individuals with ASD, their first-degree relatives, or both were eligible. The review followed PRISMA 2020. Nine reports met the eligibility criteria, comprising eight primary reports and one secondary analysis. Study-level standardized mean differences, risk ratios, and odds ratios were calculated when sufficient published data were available. No pooled meta-analysis was performed because sufficiently comparable datasets were unavailable; otherwise, findings were synthesized narratively. Serum MT protein did not differ significantly between ASD and controls in one study, whereas one small, selected gastrointestinal cohort reported more participants above a study-defined high-MT threshold. In an uncontrolled Zn supplementation study, serum MT-1A increased together with higher serum Zn and lower Cu, but the absence of a concurrent control group precluded causal attribution. Five primary reports assessed MT gene expression, with higher, lower, null, and internally inconsistent findings across different MT isoforms and blood-derived samples; no reproducible ASD-associated transcriptional pattern was identified. Anti-MT antibody findings were also inconsistent across familial, gastrointestinal, and ASD-control comparisons. Across eight primary human reports, MT-related findings in ASD were inconsistent across cohorts, biological matrices, and clinical contexts. Current evidence does not establish a consistent ASD-associated alteration of the MT system, an ASD-specific anti-MT antibody response, or a validated MT biomarker. It also does not determine whether gastrointestinal phenotype, trace-element status, redox biology, immune-related factors, or other variables explain the observed between-study differences. Larger, independently replicated studies using standardized MT measurements and well-characterized populations are required.

docs.title: Reduced dorsal CA1 activity limits retention of the temporal component of declarative memory in the Cntnap2 knockout mouse model of autism.
docs.text: Growing evidence implicates the hippocampus in the pathophysiology of autism spectrum disorder, particularly in the domains of social interactions and cognition. Yet, the mechanisms driving the hippocampal-dependent cognitive atypicalities in autism remain poorly defined. Here, we characterized how dysfunction of the CA1 subfield of the dorsal hippocampus drives abnormalities in critical components of declarative memory. Using trace fear conditioning in the Cntnap2 knockout mouse model of autism, we found that capabilities to retain the association of temporally distant stimuli (i.e. temporal binding) were reduced relative to wildtype mice. Fiber photometry and optogenetic experiments demonstrated that reduced CA1 activity during temporal gaps underlies this impairment, linking CA1 dysfunction to a deficit in long-term memory retention in autism. Using a relational/declarative memory task, we also revealed a deficit in flexible spatial memory, and a preferential use of egocentric learning strategy. This inflexible learning strategy resulted from an imbalance between memory system activity, promoting frontostriatal-dependent procedural learning instead of dorsal CA1/hippocampus-dependent relational/declarative memory. Overall, this study establishes dorsal CA1 dysfunction as a circuit-level mechanism underlying cognitive inflexibility in autism, providing a neurobiological framework for hippocampal-dependent memory deficits in the condition.

docs.title: Application of operant demand in autism and developmental disabilities: An updated review (2017-2025).
docs.text: Operant demand within behavioral economics provides a quantitative framework for evaluating reinforcer efficacy in applied research involving individuals with autism and those with related developmental disabilities. This systematic review extended the work of Gilroy, Kaplan, and Leader (2018) by examining applied operant demand research published between March 2017 and December 2025. Following PRISMA guidelines, 30 articles (31 experiments; 307 participants) were identified and coded for procedural features and methods, including operant arrangements, demand and work output analyses, open and closed economies, and unit price applications. Results indicated increased use of demand and work output analyses and unit price applications. However, open and closed economies remained rarely evaluated and substantial variability was observed in procedural methods used to manipulate price. Findings indicate growing use of operant demand analyses for treatment durability and schedule thinning but continued underuse for generalization variables.

docs.title: Emerging information technologies across the autism service and prevention continuum: a narrative review of screening, diagnosis, intervention, and health equity.
docs.text: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a major global public-health concern, yet timely identification and support remain difficult to access for many families, especially in rural, low-resource, and otherwise underserved settings. Emerging information technologies have been proposed as tools for narrowing this service gap.
