These include artificial intelligence (AI), wearable sensors, and the Internet of Things, mobile health applications and digital therapeutics, telehealth, immersive virtual and augmented reality, social robotics, and large language models. This narrative review organizes the evidence across an autism service and prevention continuum: upstream risk awareness and health education, early screening and diagnosis, and intervention, management, and long-term support. We use this continuum strictly as a public-health service-organization framework, not to imply preventing the birth or existence of autistic individuals, consistent with a neurodiversity-affirming perspective. Across each stage, we apply a health-equity lens centered on reach, affordability, scalability, health-system integration, and equity of performance. We summarize current applications, appraise recurring limitations, and synthesize cross-cutting issues of equity, data governance, ethics, neurodiversity, and implementation. Recurring limitations include small and heterogeneous studies, dataset bias, weak external validation, short follow-up, and uneven regulatory maturity. Emerging information technologies show genuine promise as complements to conventional autism services, particularly where specialist resources are scarce. Realizing population-level benefit will require equity-centered design, validation in diverse and low-resource settings, larger and longer trials, interoperable standards, and meaningful involvement of autistic people and their families.

docs.title: Feasibility and Safety of Transcranial Focused Ultrasound on Language Impairment in a Patient with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Case Report.
docs.text: Background: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is defined by persistent difficulties with social communication and language, and a subset of children stay minimally verbal despite intensive interventions. The left amygdala and ventral-anterior superior temporal sulcus (STSva) form a key circuit for social-language integration, but how transcranial focused ultrasound (tFUS) might modulate in minimally verbal ASD has not been explored. Case Presentation: An 11-year-old minimally verbal ASD boy received 4 weeks of sequential tFUS stimulation (0.5 MHz). The treatment targeted the left amygdala and STSva, five times per week. Outcome assessments included the Mandarin Clinical Evaluation of Language for Preschoolers' Core Scale (MCELP-CS), Autism Behavior Checklist (ABC), and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) at pre-tFUS, post-tFUS, and a 4-week follow-up. The boy tolerated the intervention well, with no adverse events. Significant improvements in key language skills (vocabulary naming +10%, sentence structure imitation +22%) and reduced ASD symptoms (ABC language -40%, social interaction -26%) were observed post-tFUS and sustained at follow-up. fNIRS confirmed altered cortical activation and reorganized functional connectivity in language-related brain regions. Conclusion: This single-case observational report describes acceptable tolerance to sequential tFUS targeting the left amygdala-STSva circuit in a minimally verbal child with ASD, alongside concomitant behavioural and neuroimaging changes. These preliminary observations provide descriptive, hypothesis-generating data for this circuit-directed intervention strategy and highlight the necessity of larger controlled trials to further evaluate its potential clinical utility.

docs.title: Comparison of Natural Language Processing and Traditional Qualitative Analyses of Caregiver Feedback From a Community-Based Intervention for Children With Autism.
docs.text: Background: Satisfaction data is a commonly used construct to evaluate programs, products, and experiences. This data is collected through forced choice (scales, surveys) and/or open-ended measures. While open-ended questions have the greatest potential for more useful and candid feedback, analysis of this data can be time-consuming. Objective: This paper compares two evaluation methods, traditional qualitative analysis (TQA) and Natural Language Processing (NLP), to analyze themes from open-ended satisfaction data of a caregiver-mediated intervention for families of autistic children, called 'Mind the Gap (MTG)'. Methods: This secondary analysis utilized existing survey data from 73 caregivers that participated in the MTG trial. To identify themes, TQA was performed using latent coding, and R statistical software was used for NLP, with strategies including term frequency and sentiment analysis. Methods were evaluated independently and in combination. Results And Conclusion: Both methods are comparable in thoroughly analysing this type of data, with each method contributing both unique and overlapping themes. TQA and NLP showed parent satisfaction with materials and organization, as well as peer coach support. NLP may provide more thorough results while also reducing the time burden associated with TQA, although this strategy may also overlook important nuance in data. This clinical trial is registered as 'Mind the Gap (AIRB-3) (MTG)' at clinicaltrials.gov, registration number NCT03711799.
docs.venue: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice

docs.title: Assessment of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Gender-Diverse Populations: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
docs.text: Purpose: This review aimed to determine how autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and autistic traits are assessed in gender-diverse populations. Methods: Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies published from January 2013 in English or French that focused on gender-diverse individuals and reported diagnostic procedures and/or tools used to assess ASD. Only studies involving human participants were included. Reviews, meta-analyses, case reports, editorials, posters, and conference abstracts were excluded. Two independent reviewers screened records and extracted data using a standardized form, including study design, sample characteristics, diagnostic instruments, and assessment procedures. Data were synthesized qualitatively, and pooled prevalence estimates were calculated using random-effects meta-analysis when appropriate. Methodological quality and risk of bias were assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute tools for analytical cross-sectional studies and for case-control studies. Results: Twenty-eight studies met the inclusion criteria. Eighteen assessed ASD diagnoses; only six (33%) used robust diagnostic criteria, identifying 100 participants with a confirmed ASD diagnosis (5.4%) among 1855 participants. Other studies relied mainly on self-report or screening instruments. Twenty-three studies examined the broader autism phenotype using 13 different tools. The pooled prevalence of robust ASD diagnosis was 12% (95% confidence interval [CI] = 7%-19%), and broader autism phenotype prevalence was 24% (95% CI = 17%-33%). Conclusions: Few studies met clinical gold standards. Elevated prevalence estimates may reflect methodological variability and barriers to appropriate evaluation. Training in both ASD and gender diversity is essential for inclusive and accurate diagnostic practices.

docs.title: How the Brain Interprets Pain in Autistic People: Does Sex Matter?
docs.text: Background: While psychophysical studies suggest heightened pain sensitivity in individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), the relationship between subjective pain experience and cortical neurophysiological responses and whether this relationship is sex-dependent, remains poorly understood. Methods: This cross-sectional two-group comparison study included 50 adults with Level 1 ASD and 52 age-, sex- and IQ-matched typically developing controls (TDC). Pain ratings and cortical contact heat-evoked potentials (CHEPs) were recorded in response to 52°C phasic heat stimuli. ANOVA and regression models assessed the effects of group, sex and pain ratings on CHEP amplitudes. Results: Compared to TDC, autistic participants reported higher pain scores (p = 0.004) and had lower N2 amplitudes (p = 0.02). A significant Group × Sex interaction (p < 0.001) was associated with the lowest N2 amplitudes in autistic females (p < 0.05). Regardless of group, in females, higher N2 amplitudes were associated with higher pain scores (p = 0.042; model p = 0.032), whereas this association was not significant in males (p > 0.05). Within-group correlation analyses in females showed a significant pain-N2 amplitude relationship in TDC (r = 0.734; p = 0.004) but not in autistic participants (r = 0.371; p = 0.192). Across groups and sexes, higher N2 amplitude values were associated with greater attention-to-detail autistic traits (p = 0.009). Conclusions: Our findings suggest a dissociation between subjective pain experience and cortical responses to nociceptive stimulation in autism, particularly among females, consistent with different salience-related or attentional pain processing. These results underscore the importance of considering sex and autism when interpreting pain-evoked cortical responses and challenge the assumption that pain-evoked potentials provide universally objective measures of pain. Significance: This study identifies sex-related differences in the relationship between subjective pain ratings and cortical responses to nociceptive stimulation in autistic and typically developing individuals. Autistic females showed particularly attenuated N2 amplitudes and a weaker correspondence between pain ratings and cortical responses, suggesting different salience-related or attentional processing of nociceptive stimuli. These findings highlight the importance of considering sex and autistic traits when interpreting pain-evoked cortical responses in autism.

docs.title: Gut Microbiota Composition in Helicobacter pylori-Positive Adolescents With Autism Spectrum Disorder: An Exploratory Compositional Analysis.
docs.text: Alterations in the gut microbiota have been implicated in autism spectrum disorder (ASD), but reported microbial profiles remain inconsistent, potentially because of heterogeneity in factors affecting gut microbial composition. Because Helicobacter pylori infection is associated with alterations in the gut microbiota, we investigated whether ASD was associated with gut microbial composition in a cohort of H. pylori-positive adolescents. This cross-sectional study included seven adolescents with ASD and 80 controls before H. pylori eradication therapy. Gut microbiota was analyzed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing, with alpha diversity, centered log-ratio-transformed genus-level abundance, and overall community composition based on Aitchison distance evaluated between groups. No significant differences were observed in alpha diversity or overall microbial community composition. At the genus level, 82 genera met the prevalence criterion for individual testing, and no association remained significant after false-discovery-rate correction. The effect estimate for Roseburia was not statistically significant in either unadjusted or adjusted analyses. These findings do not support marked differences in overall gut microbiota composition associated with ASD within this H. pylori-positive cohort; however, the small ASD sample and substantial age imbalance limit the precision and interpretation of the findings.
docs.venue: APMIS : acta pathologica, microbiologica, et immunologica Scandinavica

docs.title: Multidimensional Evaluation of the Efficacy of a Comprehensive Ayurveda Approach as an Add-On to Conventional Therapy in Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder: Protocol for a Randomized, Open-Label, Parallel-Group, Active-Controlled Clinical Trial.
docs.text: Background: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by impairments in social communication, restricted and repetitive behaviors, and deficits across multiple developmental domains. Although conventional interventions, including speech, behavioral, and occupational therapies, improve functional outcomes, many children continue to experience persistent cognitive and adaptive impairments. Ayurvedic formulations such as Saraswata Ghrita and Ayush Manas possess neuroprotective, anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and cognition-enhancing properties, but robust clinical evidence supporting their adjunctive use in ASD is limited. Objective: The study aims to evaluate the efficacy of a comprehensive Ayurveda intervention as an adjunct to conventional therapy in children with ASD by assessing changes in behavioral symptoms, intellectual functioning, adaptive behavior, parental quality of life, and exploratory inflammatory biomarkers. Methods: This randomized, open-label, parallel-group, active-controlled clinical trial will enroll 80 children aged 6 to 15 years diagnosed with ASD according to DSM-5 (Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition) criteria at the Central Ayurveda Research Institute (CARI), Bengaluru, in collaboration with selected autism therapy centers. Participants will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive either conventional therapy alone or conventional therapy combined with Saraswata Ghrita and Ayush Manas for 6 months. Outcome assessments will be performed at predefined intervals using the Autism Treatment Evaluation Checklist (ATEC), Indian Scale for Assessment of Autism (ISAA), Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children-Fourth Edition (WISC-IV), Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales, Third Edition (VABS-III), and Quality of Life in Autism (QoLA) questionnaire. Exploratory laboratory assessments include high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, interleukin-6, and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α). Safety will be evaluated through adverse event monitoring and laboratory investigations. Statistical analysis will be performed after data verification. Data normality will be assessed using the Shapiro-Wilk test. Variables will be represented as frequencies (%), mean (SD), or median with IQR. Preintervention and postintervention comparisons will use repeated-measures ANOVA or the Friedman test, as appropriate, with significance set at P<.05, using STATA software (version 18.0; StataCorp LLC). Results: Ethical approval was obtained before study initiation, and the trial was registered with the Clinical Trials Registry-India (CTRI/2025/04/085035). Participant recruitment commenced on December 3, 2025. As of July 17, 2026, 20 participants had been enrolled and completed baseline assessments; 14 had completed the 90-day follow-up, and 2 had completed the 6-month intervention. Recruitment is expected to continue until August 2027, followed by completion of participant follow-up, data analysis, and dissemination of study findings. Conclusions: The study will provide high-quality evidence regarding the effectiveness of integrating Ayurveda with conventional therapy for children with ASD. By simultaneously evaluating behavioral, cognitive, adaptive, quality-of-life, and exploratory biological outcomes, the trial is expected to strengthen the evidence base for multidisciplinary integrative care and inform the development of standardized treatment strategies for ASD.

docs.title: HPSC-derived mesenchymal stromal cells ameliorate murine autistic-like phenotypes through activating oxytocinergic neurons.
docs.text: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heritable neurodevelopmental disorder marked by social deficits, repetitive behaviors, and psychiatric comorbidities. Despite its rising global prevalence, effective treatments remain elusive. Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) offer therapeutic promise for ASD, although their mechanisms are unclear. Here, we show that induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived MSCs alleviate anxiety, grooming, and social impairments in Shank3B knockout mice, a monogenic ASD model. Intravenously infused MSCs localize to the neurohypophysis, interface with oxytocin (OT)-producing neuron axons, and activate OT+ neurons in the paraventricular nucleus (PVN). MSC treatment also reduces autistic-like phenotypes in BTBR T + Itpr3tf/J mice, a model of idiopathic ASD, in an OT+ neuron-dependent manner. Mechanistically, prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) secreted by MSCs instigates the activation of OT+ neuron, while suppression of PGE2 production via short hairpin RNA (shRNA)-mediated knockdown of PTGS1 and PTGES diminishes their therapeutic efficacy. These findings reveal a mechanism whereby MSCs modulate OT+ neuroendocrine circuits to improve ASD-related behaviors.

docs.title: Gray matter subtyping with SuStaIn reveals neuroanatomical patterns in autism spectrum disorder.
docs.text: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is highly heterogeneous, and structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) studies have reported both increased and decreased gray matter volume relative to typically developing controls. This variability may obscure distinct neuroanatomical patterns in conventional group-level analyses. It therefore motivates subtyping approaches that can characterize neuroanatomical heterogeneity beyond conventional group-level analyses. We applied Subtype and Stage Inference (SuStaIn) to structural MRI data from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE) to identify gray matter subtypes and stage-like variation in ASD. Original and sign-reversed z-score representations were modeled to capture gray matter deviations above and below the control reference. We then evaluated whether the organization of subtype-related brain regions was consistent across deviation directions. Cross-direction consistency, within-ABIDE cross-cohort separability, and structural covariance network (SCN) differences between stage groups were assessed using subtype alignment, Dice coefficients, cross-cohort machine-learning classification, and structural covariance analyses. We identified two gray matter subtype patterns in ASD that were consistent across deviation directions. Subtype 1 was centered on cerebellar-limbic-striatal regions, whereas Subtype 2 involved anterior fronto-cingulo-insular regions. In exploratory covariate-adjusted analyses, higher stage in sign-reversed-model S1 was associated with lower verbal intelligence quotient (IQ) scores, whereas S2 showed modestly higher Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule (ADOS) scores. The two subtypes showed regionally distinct volume profiles. The two-subtype solution showed strong cross-direction agreement, and within-ABIDE cross-cohort classification supported structural separability of the aligned subtypes. In the sign-reversed model, SCN analyses further identified stage-group structural covariance differences within each subtype, with little evidence for a stable covariance difference between subtypes. This study identifies two gray matter-based ASD subtype patterns that were consistent across the original and sign-reversed z-score representations, with distinct regional volume profiles, selective clinical associations, and stage-group structural covariance differences. The findings provide a neuroanatomical framework for organizing ASD heterogeneity and for examining brain-behavior variation in future studies.

docs.title: Exploring the Neural Mechanisms of Acupuncture Stimulation in Autism Spectrum Disorder: Protocol for a Randomized, Sham-Controlled, Multimodal Neuroimaging Trial.
docs.text: Background: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by restricted and repetitive behaviors and disturbances in social communication and interaction. Currently, there is no fundamental treatment for ASD, with only a few medications available for use on a limited basis to manage concomitant neuropsychiatric symptoms. The primary therapeutic goal of such treatments is to alleviate symptoms while maximizing the functional independence and quality of life of affected individuals. Many complementary and alternative medicine therapies have been reported to have effects on ASD symptoms; however, evidence is insufficient to confirm their clinical effectiveness. Acupuncture has traditionally been used as a complementary intervention to manage various neurological and neuropsychiatric diseases, including ASD, in East Asia. However, how acupuncture stimulation modulates neural activity at the macroscale level in individuals with ASD remains largely unknown. Objective: This study aims to elucidate disease-related brain alterations and explore the acute neural mechanisms underlying acupuncture stimulation in patients with ASD and in typically developing (TD) individuals, using a multimodal neuroimaging approach. Methods: This study was designed as a randomized, sham-controlled trial. In this stratified 2×2 design, 70 participants, including individuals with ASD (n=35) and TD controls (n=35), will each be randomly assigned to either the verum or sham acupuncture group, resulting in 4 groups. The verum acupuncture group will receive stimulation at specific acupoints clinically indicated for ASD, eliciting a deqi sensation. The sham acupuncture group will receive superficial needling at nonacupoints unrelated to ASD symptoms. Each group will undergo clinical assessments and multimodal neuroimaging measurements, including functional near-infrared spectroscopy and electroencephalography, before and after acupuncture stimulation. The primary outcome will be differences in resting state network metrics and relative band power in frontal areas by disease status. Secondary outcomes will include differences in these neural markers following acupuncture stimulation between the verum and sham groups, reflecting the group × intervention interaction. Exploratory outcomes will focus on identifying neural markers that correlate with clinical indicators of ASD. Results: Recruitment began in April 2025. To date, 23 individuals with ASD and 21 TD individuals have participated in this study. The recruitment process is expected to continue until December 2026. Conclusions: ASD presents a significant socioeconomic burden, with no definitive treatment established to date. Although acupuncture is a widely applied intervention for various neurological conditions, including ASD, its large-scale neural mechanisms remain poorly understood. By using multimodal neuroimaging, the present study aims to investigate the immediate neural substrates underlying acupuncture stimulation in patients with ASD. These findings are expected to provide a robust neurobiological foundation for future longitudinal research and the development of evidence-based integrative strategies.

docs.title: An Effective Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Framework Using Adaptive Serial Hybrid Network With Self-Calibrated Feature Extraction on Brain MRI Images.
docs.text: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a medical condition commonly categorized as a neurodevelopmental disorder. Patients with ASD are not limited to common symptoms, and it often requires long-term hospital visits and specialists for definitive evaluation. Research has highlighted the importance of early intervention and care for ASD patients, as it can benefit their lifestyle. Automated detection techniques through deep learners have shown great progress in detecting ASD, as they excel in handling highly complex features and functional activity patterns by evaluating magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). However, as the ASD-associated neuroimaging patterns are not explicitly shown in the MRI, several challenges remain in identifying the ASD related features from MRI evaluation. To overcome these challenges, an advanced deep learning framework has been developed for detecting ASD. In this proposed model, MRI scans are collected from accessible datasets and applied to the feature extraction process. Here, feature extraction was carried out with the support of the proposed Self-Calibrated Dense Convolution Vision Transformer (SC-DCVT). This proposed feature extraction model integrates dense connections and self-calibration mechanisms to capture rich, contextual features from the MRI images, improving the representation of complex patterns. Then, the extracted features are fed to the proposed Adaptive Serial Hybrid Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Network (ASHASDDetN) model, which integrates two components, such as Residual-Temporal Convolutional Network (Res-TCN) with Dense Conditional Random Field (DCRF), to process ASD detection by capturing relevant features and ensuring its consistency. The reliability of the proposed ASHASDDetN model is enhanced by optimizing the parameters of Res-TCN and DCRF with the support of the Improved Position Updating Actor Optimization Algorithm (IPU-AOA) for the ASD detection task. The effectiveness of the proposed model is proven by conducting extensive experimentation among state-of-the-art techniques.
docs.venue: International journal of developmental neuroscience : the official journal of the International Society for Developmental Neuroscience

docs.title: Considering Autism in Binge-Type Eating Disorders: Broadening Beyond an Anorexia Nervosa-Focused Model.
docs.text: Purpose Of Review: Research on Autism in eating disorders (EDs) has historically focused on anorexia nervosa (AN), with comparatively limited attention given to binge-type EDs such as bulimia nervosa (BN) and binge eating disorder (BED). This review summarises emerging evidence on Autism in binge-type EDs and highlights key clinical and research implications. Recent Findings: Emerging evidence suggests that Autism is over-represented in BN and BED, although prevalence appears lower than in AN and research remains methodologically limited. Recent studies suggest that affective and reward-related processes, alongside sensory differences, may contribute to binge-type presentations. Co-occurring ADHD appears particularly relevant and may complicate recognition, clinical presentation, and treatment. Autism also remains under-recognised in binge-type EDs by ED services, where existing adaptations remain largely derived from AN models. Current AN-centric models may inadequately capture Neurodivergence in binge-type EDs. More transdiagnostic, mechanism-informed research and treatment approaches are needed.

docs.title: Therapeutic Horseback Riding for Youth With Autism and Psychiatric Comorbidities: A Randomized Trial.
docs.text: Objective: Autism spectrum disorder care is often complicated by co-occurring psychiatric symptoms. Equine-assisted services show promise for improving behavioral outcomes in this population. We aimed to examine benefits of equine-assisted services for youth with autism at higher risk for mental health interventions. Methods: A total of 236 youth with autism and psychiatric comorbidity (aged 6-16 years.) were enrolled in a randomized controlled multisite clinical trial, stratified by nonverbal IQ, and assigned to 1 of 3 intervention arms: therapeutic horseback riding (THR), no horse contact barn activity (BA), or waiting period followed by a BA/THR hybrid. Caregivers completed outcome measures. Speech outcomes were evaluated by blinded raters. Intervention methods expand those from a previous efficacy trial. Results: Intent-to-treat analyses with 169 participants completing at least 1 intervention lesson revealed that compared with the waitlist control (n = 28), both THR (n = 74) and BA (n = 67) interventions showed clinically significant reductions in co-primary outcomes of irritability (P < .0001; THR effect size d = 1.15; BA effect size d = 1.04) and hyperactivity (THR P < .0001, effect size d = 1.06; BA P = .005, effect size d = 0.68). The THR group showed significantly greater reductions in hyperactivity compared with the BA group (P = .03; effect size d = 0.39) beginning at intervention week 4. Additional significant improvements in THR and BA groups vs the waitlist control were seen in emotional regulation and social behaviors. Conclusions: Equine-assisted activities are an effective intervention to address behavior challenges in youth with autism and psychiatric comorbidity; THR may offer additive reductions in hyperactivity.

docs.title: Drosophila prickle mutants display comorbid neurological phenotypes and present with autism spectrum disorder-associated phenotypes.
docs.text: Epilepsy affects approximately 30% of individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Consistent with these observations, while PRICKLE mutations are primarily linked with epilepsy, there is an enrichment of pathogenic DNA sequence variants in PRICKLE genes carried by individuals with ASD. Nonetheless, a connection between PRICKLE function and ASD warrants further investigation. Here, we show that a seizure-prone Drosophila prickle mutant (prickle-spiny-legs, or pksple) exhibits learning and memory deficits, increased pain sensitivity, both communication and social interaction difficulties, and restrictive repetitive grooming behaviors, all of which are strongly correlated with ASD, while a non-seizure prone prickle mutant (prickle-prickle, or pkpk) does not, thereby associating epilepsy and ASD through prickle. Comparing headed versus headless pksple mutants, we also show that the excessive grooming requires higher level cognitive processing from the brain. Finally, both pksple and pkpk mutants exhibit circadian rhythm defects, another feature correlated with ASD, as well as distinct yet overlapping neurological anomalies in processes that include innate immune response, oxidative stress response, neuronal cell death, neurodegeneration, motor dysfunction and reduced lifespan, likely reflecting the unique isoform expression patterns observed in the developing CNS. Collectively, this study highlights the broadscale effects of PRICKLE mutations that extend beyond the primary clinical features of epilepsy to include several of the core features of ASD.

docs.title: Toward Scalable Driver Readiness Screenings for Autistic Teens: Clinical Measures Correlated With Real-World Evaluations.
docs.text: ImportanceThere are no standardized pathways to guide autistic adolescents through the learning-to-drive process, beginning with deciding whether they are ready to pursue driving.ObjectiveTo examine whether commonly used clinical assessments correlate with driver readiness determinations.DesignCross-sectional, nonexperimental study using a single in-person visit comprised of a clinical assessment and on-road passenger activities.SettingA primary care clinic in an urban city.ParticipantsTwenty-one autistic adolescents aged 15-19 years without a learner's permit were recruited via email outreach. Inclusion criteria required English fluency and ability to complete an in-person 4-h visit.Outcomes and MeasuresParticipants completed a clinical battery and on-road passenger activities. Readiness determinations were dichotomized into "Not Ready" or "Ready" for a formal driver evaluation. We conducted descriptive statistics, correlations, and positive predictive and negative predictive value tests to assess differences by clinical measures scores and readiness determinations.ResultsSeven participants were categorized as "Not Ready" and 14 as "Ready." Strongest correlations with readiness were observed for Bruininks-Oseretsky Test of Motor Proficiency, Second Edition (BOT-2) Short Form scores and Beery Visual-Motor Integration (VMI) scores. Potential cut points between groups included <22 on the Beery VMI raw score, >65 on the BOT-2 Total Point Score, >36 on the BOT-2 Standard Score, and ≥5 on the BOT-2 Transferring Pennies score. NIH Toolbox working memory and cognitive flexibility tasks showed moderate associations.Conclusions and RelevanceCommonly used clinical assessments show preliminary associations with driver readiness outcomes. Findings support future development of a standardized screening battery to guide referral decisions and predriving skill development.
docs.venue: The American journal of occupational therapy : official publication of the American Occupational Therapy Association

docs.title: The utility of animal models in hiPSC-based studies of autism spectrum disorder: a systematic review.
docs.text: Introduction: Autism spectrum disorder is a highly prevalent and heritable neurodevelopmental condition. To investigate its pathogenesis, genetic and non-genetic animal models have been developed. However, no animal model can fully capture the human-specific characteristics and genetic complexity of autism spectrum disorder. In this context, human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC) derived models have emerged as powerful tools in autism spectrum disorder research, offering the potential to reduce or replace animal experiments. Despite this potential, many hiPSC-based studies still incorporate animal use. Objective: To analyze the use of animals in hiPSC-based studies of autism spectrum disorder, with the aim of assessing the necessity of their inclusion and their contribution to our understanding of disease mechanisms. Methods: Following the PRISMA guidelines, we searched PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science for articles published between 2009 and 2024 using the search terms "autism", "ASD", and "autism spectrum disorder" combined with "iPSC", "induced pluripotent stem cells and "organoid*". Results: A total of 207 studies using hiPSCs to investigate Autism spectrum disorder were identified. Of these, 79 studies (38.16%) also involved animals or animal-derived cells. While nearly half of these studies used autism spectrum disorder animal models to explore neurobiological mechanisms of the disorder, the remaining studies employed animals for purposes not directly related to understanding autism spectrum disorder pathophysiology. These included teratoma formation assays to validate hiPSC pluripotency and the extraction of primary astrocytes for co-culture with hiPSC-derived neurons, an approach that may introduce confounding variables. Conclusion: Our review highlights the frequent and, in some cases, unnecessary use of animals in hiPSC-based studies of autism spectrum disorder.

docs.title: From the emergence of psychiatry to neoliberal logic: the commodification of contemporary suffering.
docs.text: This study discusses the concepts of normality and pathologization in contemporaneity from a historical context of the emergence and growth of psychiatry associated with the development of neoliberalism. The psychiatric knowledge begins to grown allied to an economic management of the government, transforming the suffering in commodity. Therefore, the psychiatric reform face challenges against the asylum logic, still present in society, which seeks to catalog diseases and diagnose natural issues of everyday life. Thus, we seek to understand how neoliberal logic is associated with psychiatric knowledge and consequently influences the increase in diagnoses of mental disorders in contemporary times. To achieve this goal, we analyzed journalistic articles and scientific research that address the increase in diagnoses of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and Attention Deficit with Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD). It was concluded that it is still necessary to question the influences of psychiatric knowledge and the pharmaceutical industry on what is transmitted to society regarding this subject.

docs.title: Disparities in Autism Spectrum Disorder and Perinatal Risk Factors.
docs.text: Importance: In universal health care settings, trends in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) diagnosis remain poorly characterized, yet are critical for identifying inequities that persist despite more equitable health care access. Objective: To describe temporal trends in ASD diagnosis and in perinatal risk factors for ASD across maternal socioeconomic and immigration factors. Design, Setting, And Participants: This is a population-based retrospective cohort study of children born in Ontario, Canada (2002-2020), linked to maternal health, immigration, and census data. Children were followed up from age 1 year until ASD diagnosis, death, out-migration, or April 2020. Data analysis was performed between August 2024 and March 2026. Exposures: Maternal socioeconomic indicators (area-level deprivation, ethnic diversity, income, Ontario Drug Benefit enrollment, and rural vs urban residence) and immigration characteristics (immigration status, category, time since immigration, region of origin, and country income level). Perinatal risk factors included maternal diabetes, maternal age 35 years or older, severe maternal morbidity, and prematurity. Main Outcomes And Measures: ASD was identified using a validated administrative algorithm. Incidence rates were calculated per 10 000 person-years and cumulative incidence per 1000 live births at 8 years. Temporal trends were estimated using negative binomial regression with interaction terms between birth year and covariates. Results: Of 2 319 302 children (1 188 270 male [51.2%]), 29 374 (1.3%) met ASD criteria, with 80.0% (23 068 children) receiving a diagnosis by age 8 years and 78.5% of cases (23 071 cases) occurring in male children. Diagnosis increased by 10% per birth cohort (95% CI, 10%-11%). Disparities in ASD diagnosis by socioeconomic and immigration characteristics widened across birth cohorts: by the 2012 birth cohort, diagnosis was 2.2-fold (95% CI, 2.0-2.4-fold) higher in the most vs least deprived neighborhoods, 2.0-fold (95% CI, 1.8-2.2-fold) higher in the most vs least ethnically diverse areas, and lower in rural vs urban regions. Diagnosis was 1.4-fold (95% CI, 1.3-1.5-fold) higher among children of immigrant mothers, with the highest rates among mothers from low- and middle-income regions. Diabetes during pregnancy, severe maternal morbidity, and prematurity were more common in marginalized populations, with disparities in maternal diabetes widening over time. Conclusions And Relevance: In this cohort study of more than 2.3 million mother-child pairs, ASD diagnoses occurred disproportionately among children from socioeconomically disadvantaged and immigrant families, with disparities widening over time. The higher prevalence of maternal diabetes, obstetric complications, and prematurity in these populations may have contributed to these differences.

docs.title: Cerebral Lateralization for Language as a Potential Biomarker for the Broad Autism Phenotype: A Functional Transcranial Doppler Ultrasonography Investigation.
docs.text: Introduction: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is associated with language deficits, while growing evidence suggests that atypical cerebral lateralization for language could serve as a potential neural marker for ASD. The present study seeks to investigate cerebral lateralization for language not only in terms of ASD, but also as a potential biomarker for the broad autism phenotype (BAP)-a sum of subclinical traits similar to those of ASD. BAP is often observed in family members of individuals with ASD, and encompasses personality, linguistic, social, communicative, and behavioral challenges that fall short of the diagnostic threshold for ASD. We hypothesize that individuals with ASD will show atypical patterns of cerebral lateralization for language relative to neurotypical controls, with individuals exhibiting BAP characteristics expected to fall between these two groups. Methods: To test this hypothesis, neurophysiological and behavioral assessments of cerebral lateralization for language, alongside cerebral lateralization of visuospatial functions-to confirm that the expected differences are specific to language lateralization-will be performed in at least 26 children and adults with high-functioning ASD, 26 BAP-positive siblings (BAP group), and 26 neurotypical controls. Behavioral lateralization, namely handedness, will be assessed through neuropsychological tools, while cerebral lateralization will be measured utilizing functional transcranial Doppler ultrasonography (fTCD), a validated and reliable tool specialized for cerebral lateralization assessment. Results: This is a Stage-1 registered report; therefore, no results are available at this time point. Conclusion: Findings are expected to inform improved understanding and, potentially, early identification and screening for both ASD and BAP.

docs.title: Spaciousness as an acoustic measure of prosody in autistic children.
docs.text: Distinctive prosody has been reported in autism, yet acoustic studies have yielded inconsistent findings, particularly for F0-related measures. Two dynamic measures, spaciousness (magnitude of pitch excursions) and wiggliness (rate of pitch-direction changes), offer alternatives, but spaciousness has not yet been applied to English-speaking autistic children. The present study therefore compared acoustic characteristics of prosody from autistic and language-skill matched nonautistic children (age 3-7) using spaciousness, wiggliness, F0 measures (mean, standard deviation, and range), and speech rate. Linear mixed-effects models revealed that only spaciousness showed significant group differences, and these differences were independent of utterance length. Replication in larger samples is warranted.

docs.title: Recent Advances in Autism Spectrum Disorder Research on Epigenetics and Personalised Medicine.
docs.text: Background: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a multifaceted neurodevelopmental condition characterised by impairments in social interaction and communication, repetitive and restricted patterns of behaviour and atypical sensory processing. Although genetic susceptibility accounts for a substantial proportion of ASD risk, increasing evidence indicates that epigenetic modifications and environmental exposures play pivotal roles in disease development and progression. Purpose: This review provides an updated overview of the current understanding of ASD pathogenesis, focusing on the interplay between epigenetic regulation, maternal health and the gut microbiome. It also highlights emerging diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic strategies that have the potential to enhance early diagnosis and improve clinical management. Main Findings: Recent studies indicate that maternal immune dysregulation, nutritional status, metabolic disorders and alterations in the maternal gut microbiota during pregnancy may contribute to ASD risk by inducing epigenetic changes and disrupting neurodevelopmental pathways. At the same time, novel pharmacological interventions aimed at alleviating behavioural symptoms and targeting epigenetic mechanisms are being actively explored. Advances in diagnostic technologies, including saliva-based microRNA profiling and epigenetic biomarkers, offer promising opportunities for earlier and more accurate ASD detection. Furthermore, genome-wide analyses and multi-omics approaches are facilitating the development of personalised diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. Conclusion: Despite considerable progress in elucidating the genetic and environmental factors associated with ASD, the disorder remains highly heterogeneous and biologically complex. Future research integrating epigenetic insights, microbiome investigations and precision medicine approaches will be crucial for uncovering the underlying molecular mechanisms and translating these discoveries into more effective diagnostic tools and targeted therapies.

docs.title: A multi-atlas ensemble learning framework for autism spectrum disorder diagnosis.
docs.text: Objective.Clinical autism spectrum disorder (ASD) relies on subjective scales and neuroimaging, with traditional approaches suffering from high subjectivity and insufficient feature extraction, increasing misdiagnoses risk.Approach.To improve the diagnostic accuracy, we propose a multimodal ASD prediction network (APN) that integrates resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging with non-imaging data. Algorithmically, we first introduce a novel cumulative distribution divergence score (CDDS) feature selection method based on the multi-atlas functional connectivity (FC), which quantifies statistical distributional differences between positive and negative samples, effectively addressing the limitations of the traditionalF-score in overlapping or weakly discriminative features. Building upon this, we adapt existing deep learning (DL) paradigms to construct a deep neural architecture (variational autoencoder-denoising autoencoder (VAEA)), combining a variational autoencoder (VAE), a denoising autoencoder, and a multilayer perceptron. The combination of these modules is non-trivial: the novel CDDS first purifies the high-dimensional feature space, enabling the VAEA to learn robust latent probabilistic representations via unsupervised pre-training without suffering from the curse of dimensionality. This is followed by the supervised fine-tuning to optimize parameters. We further incorporate demographic factors including age, full-scale intelligence quotient, and gender via a late-fusion strategy to prevent them from being overshadowed by imaging features, thereby enhancing the discriminability. FC features from three atlases including AAL, CC400, and Dosenbach160 are weighted and integrated to achieve the effective multi-source fusion.Main results.We conduct 10-fold cross-validations on the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE) dataset, and the proposed APN achieves 81.63% accuracy, 81.89% sensitivity and 81.46% specificity, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art methods. Interpretability analysis identifies hippocampus, amygdala, and cingulate gyrus as strongly ASD-associated regions, offering neural mechanistic insights.Significance.This study provides an efficient, objective, and interpretable multimodal DL framework for ASD assisted diagnosis, with substantial clinical application and neuroscience value.

docs.title: Sleep Problems and Mental Health in Middle-Aged and Older Autistic and Non-Autistic Adults.
docs.text: Background: Sleep is a vital biological function, and impaired sleep can lead to a range of problems, including poor health and wellbeing. Poor sleep and higher rates of sleep-related problems and difficulties are often reported by autistic people of all ages, however, these experiences and problems have seldom been studied in diagnosed autistic populations in midlife and old age. Methods: This study used data from the first wave of the AgeWellAutism cohort, from a sample of 265 autistic and 167 age- and gender-matched non-autistic adults aged 40-93 years (mean = ∼60 years; ∼50% female). Participants completed widely used and standardised measures of sleep quality and mental health symptoms. Results: The autistic group reported significantly greater sleep problems than the non-autistic group, with poorer overall sleep across all domains (all p < 0.001), with autistic women reporting greatest difficulties. The largest differences between groups were observed in sleep disturbances and daytime dysfunction (χ2 = 101.8 and 95.1, respectively, both p < 0.001). These differences remained significant after controlling for age and symptoms of anxiety, depression and PTSD. Across both groups, poorer sleep was associated with older age and higher levels of anxiety, depression and PTSD symptoms, with a stronger association between sleep problems and anxiety symptoms in the autistic group. Conclusions: Consistent with prior autism trait-based research in the general population, middle-aged and older autistic adults report more extensive sleep problems and worse sleep quality than non-autistic adults. Sleep problems were associated with older age and poorer mental health. Though the study is cross-sectional, the findings highlight the need to explore causal links through intervention. Addressing anxiety, and mental health problems more broadly, may improve sleep quality in ageing autistic populations.

docs.title: Pathological Priming and Developmental Heterochrony as Organizing Concepts in Human iPSC Models of Autism Spectrum Disorder.
docs.text: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition in which diverse genetic risk factors converge on molecular pathways governing early brain development. Human-induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) and brain organoid models now permit direct interrogation of these pathways in patient-derived neural tissue and, in a subset of studies, reveal alterations in neural progenitor proliferation, cortical neurogenesis, synaptic maturation, and network excitability. A landmark iPSC study in macrocephalic idiopathic ASD introduced the concept of pathological priming of neural progenitors, durable reconfiguration of chromatin and transcriptional states that biases downstream developmental programs, and associated developmental heterochrony in neuronal gene networks, thereby linking early progenitor biology to selectively shifted trajectories of neuronal maturation and to macrostructural and functional abnormalities. This conceptual review synthesizes evidence for pathological priming and developmental heterochrony from human iPSC-derived neurons and brain organoids, focusing on the ASD subgroups in which timing mechanisms are best supported: macrocephalic idiopathic ASD, 16p11.2 and related copy number variants, and large-effect developmental regulators such as SYNGAP1. We summarize recurrent and inconsistent cellular and circuit phenotypes, evaluate multi-omic data implicating progenitor regulatory states in shaping developmental timing, and situate timing-focused mechanisms alongside synaptopathy, excitatory-inhibitory imbalance, critical-period, and neuroimmune models. We propose that disturbances in neurodevelopmental timing characterize specific ASD subgroups, particularly those with early brain overgrowth or large-effect developmental regulators, rather than ASD as a whole, and offer a useful organizing principle for integrating divergent findings and generating testable, timing-informed hypotheses for future experimental and translational work.

docs.title: Effects of High-Phenolic Extra Virgin Olive Oil on Sensory Processing in Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Pilot Study.
docs.text: No approved treatments currently exist for the core symptoms of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), prompting clinicians and families to seek alternative approaches, including dietary and nutritional interventions. The Mediterranean diet (MeDi), characterized by a high intake of antioxidant and anti-inflammatory components, is associated with improved health outcomes and reduced risk of chronic diseases. A key element of the MeDi is extra virgin olive oil (EVOO), which is rich in bioactive phenolics, including oleocanthal, oleuropein and hydroxytyrosol. Through its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory actions, EVOO may contribute to regulating pathological processes in both the central nervous system (CNS) and the gastrointestinal tract, offering a promising avenue for pharmacological and nutritional intervention in children with ASD. This pilot study investigated the effects of a three-month intervention combining the MeDi with EVOO supplementation on ASD symptoms. Ten children diagnosed with ASD aged 5.00-11.7 years, all boys, were recruited from Northern Greece. The changes in social interaction and communication were evaluated using standardized instruments: the Social Responsiveness Scale (SRS), Word Finding Vocabulary Test (WFVT), Autism Diagnostic Interview-Revised (ADI-R) and the Sensory Profile (SP). Paired-sample t-tests revealed significant improvements post-intervention in SRS (p = 0.034), ADI-R A (p = 0.008), WFVT (p = 0.020) and ADI-R B (p = 0.022) scores. These findings suggest that EVOO supplementation may reduce the severity of social deficits and enhance communication skills in children with ASD.
